summary: For a continuous (gaussian/MD) outcome with both threshold spellings left unset, both DINA routes take the harm floor from the raw formal hr.threshold = 1.25 instead of the resolved MD screening threshold 0.0, so the fit builds its candidate family under a 1.25-outcome-unit floor while the returned object reports a floor of 0 and every bootstrap/CV replay of args_call_all runs DINA with floor 0. Also at: forestsearch_main.R:3237 (use_dina screening, selected_only = TRUE: m_diff_sel <- hr.threshold for gaussian); forestsearch_helpers.R:1525 (consumer: m_diff <- hr.threshold for gaussian); documentation the code contradicts: forestsearch_main.R:446-449 and :1268, dina_subgroup.R:144-146, NEWS.md:1109-1112 and :520-541; forestsearch_helpers.R:1525
fix_summary: Derive the DINA floor at both sites (the subgroup_method = "dina" call and the use_dina selected-cut screening) from the resolved natural-scale screening threshold that is recorded in threshold_config and written to args_call_all$effect.threshold, not from the raw hr.threshold formal.

summary: On the default consistency path forestsearch() attaches treat.recommend to df.est and df.predict by a merge on the id column, so inside every full-bootstrap replicate (resample keeps the original ids, repeated k_i times) df.est has k_i^2 rows per subject and df.predict is the in-bag subjects only (k_i copies each, out-of-bag subjects NA), which makes the replicate's 'new subgroup on original data' estimate the bootstrap-sample estimate and its 'new subgroup on bootstrap data' estimate a k_i^2-weighted one. Also at: forestsearch_main.R:3733 (df.predict merge); flag table subgroup_consistency_helpers.R:939-942; consumers bootstrap_analysis_dofuture.R:629-630, 651, 667, 688-697, 700-711, 726-728, 741-769, 872-875, 889; reported through bootstrap_dofuture_main.R:573-601; bootstrap_analysis_dofuture.R:438; forestsearch_main.R:3722
fix_summary: On the consistency path attach treat.recommend to df.est by row position and to df.predict by evaluating the selected subgroup definition on its rows (as df.test and the DINA/GRF branches already do) instead of joining on id.

summary: For a replicate under an alternative DGM in which nothing is identified, the simulation extractors store spec = |Hc|/N (the value of NPV for an empty identified set) where specificity is 1, so the all-replicate specificity shown by the exported OC summaries is too low by about (1 - detection rate) x |H|/N; npv is stored as 1, which matches the table-fill convention but not the found-case formula. Also at: run_simulation_analysis.R:1026 (npv = 1), :1066, :1392, :1418 (same assignments in the three other nothing-found branches; :1392 and :1418 are in .extract_grf_estimates_gen); consumers that average the stored value over all replicates: simulation_tables.R:379 (sens(Hc)) and :381 (ppv(Hc)), oc_analyses.R:457 (summarize_single_analysis), oc_analyses.R:688 and :690 (format_oc_results); fill made dead by the stored value: simulation_tables.R:371-372 (stale comment :366-367)
fix_summary: Store spec = 1 in the four nothing-found branches under an alternative, and choose one package-wide value for npv in that case (1, as the table fill and fs_mr_oc_summary use, or |Hc|/N, as the found-case formula gives).

summary: The exported generate_gbsg_bootstrap_general() loads its source data with data("gbsg", package = "survival"), which loads nothing with survival 3.8-12 (gbsg ships inside the cancer data file), so gbsg stays NULL and every call, including the default call, stops with "'data' must be a data frame".
fix_summary: Take the data from survival::gbsg, as the package's other examples do.

summary: get_Cox_sg() fits coxph() under suppressWarnings() with no per-arm event check, so a slice with a zero-event arm is expected to return a large finite log-HR that passes the bootstrap's is.finite() guard, whereas the search scorer and .make_cox_estimator() return non-estimable for the same slice. Also at: bootstrap_analysis_dofuture.R:478, :507 (the two calls that can meet a zero-event arm: original H / Hc evaluated on a resample); bootstrap_analysis_dofuture.R:724, :767 (guards test is.finite only); Cox_estimation_helpers.R:194-196 (fit_cox_models)
fix_summary: Apply the existing per-arm existence check (.fs_existence_reason for HR) inside get_Cox_sg(), or in its bootstrap callers, and return NA for a non-estimable slice so the draw is dropped like a non-finite one.

summary: When the exported bootstrap_results() is called directly with its default boot_index_mat = NULL, it draws the resampling indices from per-iteration doFuture RNG streams and does not return them, while bootstrap_ystar() with the same seed draws a different Mersenne-Twister index set, so a direct caller who pairs the two in get_dfRes() (the route the @seealso and the wrapper's seed documentation point to) gets an IJ variance computed against unrelated multiplicities, with no error. Also at: bootstrap_dofuture_main.R:30-36 (stale @param seed: the wrapper no longer calls bootstrap_ystar()); bootstrap_analysis_dofuture.R:250-251 (@seealso), 344-346 (comment), 101-111 (@param boot_index_mat); bootstrap_calculations_helpers.R:103-106
fix_summary: Return the indices actually used (or require boot_index_mat for direct callers) and correct the @seealso, the wrapper's @param seed and the in-code comment that promise seed alignment with bootstrap_ystar().

summary: The four event counts for the original subgroup on each resample (events_H_0, events_H_1, events_Hc_0, events_Hc_1) are computed and then overwritten with NA before the result row is built, so these documented columns are NA on every replicate and summarize_bootstrap_events() always reports zero low-event resamples for the original H and Hc. Also at: bootstrap_analysis_dofuture.R:535-537 (the other three overwrites); :916-919 (written to the row); :133-136 (roxygen documents integer counts); bootstrap_summaries_helpers.R:1091-1103 (consumer)
fix_summary: Remove the four re-initialisations at :534-537, or move the NA initialisation block above the computation at :464.

summary: A bootstrap replicate whose inner forestsearch() call throws is recorded exactly like a replicate that found no subgroup (NA estimates, any_found = 0), its warning is suppressed twice, and if every replicate throws the user is told the selection criteria were not reached. Also at: bootstrap_analysis_dofuture.R:408 (suppressWarnings around the foreach); bootstrap_analysis_dofuture.R:619-621 (the warning that is never seen); bootstrap_dofuture_main.R:346-347 (options(warn = -1)); bootstrap_dofuture_main.R:532-539 (misattributing message); bootstrap_analysis_dofuture.R:230 (roxygen says 'Warns')
fix_summary: Record each replicate's caught error (a column or attribute) and report the count and first message after the loop, outside the suppressed section.

summary: For GLM outcomes the bootstrap rebuilds its effect estimator from the stored call without adverse_outcome and without ps_adjust_method, so its observed and bias-corrected estimates are on the unflipped, unweighted scale even when the search that selected the subgroup used adverse_outcome = FALSE (the resolved default for continuous outcomes) or propensity adjustment. Also at: mr_estimates_table.R:204-208 (same omission, but the effect column is then overwritten from fs$mr_inference at :283-286); forestsearch_cross_validation.R:1452-1458, 1508-1515 (reader's citation, not re-verified); forestsearch_main.R:2705-2712 (the PS rebuild of the search estimator itself omits adverse_outcome)
fix_summary: Pass the recorded adverse_outcome and ps_adjust_method when rebuilding the bootstrap estimator, or document that the bootstrap reports on the natural (unflipped, unweighted) scale.

summary: The success guard covers only zero re-identifying replicates; with exactly one, the infinitesimal-jackknife standard error is exactly 0 and a zero-width bias-corrected interval is reported with no warning. Also at: bootstrap_calculations_helpers.R:345-346, 351, 360-371 (get_targetEst returns sehat_new = 0); bootstrap_calculations_helpers.R:156 (ci_est accepts sd = 0)
fix_summary: Treat fewer than two usable replicates as having no variance estimate (NA interval with a warning) instead of returning a zero standard error.

summary: For a survival fit made with est.scale = "1/hr", each row of the bootstrap summary table FSsg_tab pairs one subgroup's label, counts, medians and unadjusted estimate with the other subgroup's bias-corrected estimate (the Qstnbl row, which holds H = treat.recommend == 0, shows Hc_bc, and the Recmnd row shows H_bc). Also at: bootstrap_dofuture_main.R:737 (paired assignment); consumers that inherit the mis-paired rows: bootstrap_summaries_helpers.R:237-249 (footnote ties the Qstnbl row to sg.harm), mr_estimates_table.R:101-114 (locates the H row by the string SG_CIs$H_bc)
fix_summary: On est.scale = "1/hr" pass each bias-corrected string to its own subgroup's row (H_bc with treat.recommend == 0, Hc_bc with treat.recommend == 1) and, if the reversed reading is wanted, swap the two row labels as the cross-validation and KM-plot code do.

summary: For a Cox model with more than one coefficient (a linear adjust_covariates term such as "x2") the treatment dfbeta column is looked up by column name, but survival's dfbeta residual matrix has no column names, so the function returns NULL for every candidate and the resample approximation and MR pieces are silently unavailable. Also at: subgroup_consistency_helpers.R:1491-1500 and :1885-1890 (silent fallback to literal splitting); fs_mr_inference.R:96-97 and :637-641 (every candidate dropped, MR returns a note with harm_flag NA); forestsearch_main.R:3830 (MR keeps exactly the plain-column adjusters)
fix_summary: Select the treatment column of the dfbeta matrix by position matched against names(coef(fit)) rather than by the matrix's column names.

summary: Cross-fit coefficients are combined with colMeans(beta_mat, na.rm = TRUE), so a step-2 coefficient that is aliased (NA) in one fold is silently replaced by the other fold's estimate alone, and one that is NA in every fold becomes NaN, is returned without error, and later makes dina_subgroup() fail with 'missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed'. Also at: dina.R:852 (glm.fit NA coefficient passed on unchecked); dina.R:911-923 (coxph NA coefficient; singular-information branch returns an NA sigma); dina_subgroup.R:749 and :888 (if (mean_tau < m_diff) errors on NaN)
fix_summary: Detect NA step-2 coefficients per fold and stop or warn naming the covariate instead of averaging over the remaining folds, and have dina_subgroup() reject a fit with non-finite coefficients with a clear message.

summary: dina_fit(family = "gaussian", baseline_method = list(eta0 = , eta1 = )) is documented and passes validation but always stops with 'could not find function "nu_fn"', because the eta0/eta1 list branch returns nu_fn = NULL and the Gaussian nuisance combiner evaluates only nu_fn. Also at: dina.R:766 (the failing call nu_fn(X_new) with nu_fn bound to NULL); dina.R:86-89 (roxygen documenting the eta0/eta1 list with no family restriction); dina.R:508-509 (stop text that also implies eta0/eta1 is accepted for every non-Cox family); same failure via dina_fit_bagged() (dina_bagged.R:348-352; caught per bag at dina_bagged.R:381-403, so all bags fail and the function stops at dina_bagged.R:262-263) and via dina() / dina_bagged() / dina_subgroup_bootstrap(), which forward baseline_method through ... (dina_df.R:98-102, dina_df.R:179-183, dina_subgroup_bootstrap.R:182-184)
fix_summary: For the Gaussian family with an eta0/eta1 list, either build nu(x) from the supplied functions and the propensity (the a*eta1 + (1 - a)*eta0 combination already used for the other families, with a = e) or reject that list up front with an explicit message and correct the roxygen and the stop text.

summary: cens_type = "unknown" fits one pooled logistic model of status on X and returns the same function for both arms, so the two not-censoring probabilities cancel in a(x) and the option gives the same estimator as cens_type = NULL up to the eps = 1e-6 stabiliser. Also at: dina.R:648-659 (single pooled fit, no arm term); dina.R:801-805 (identical probabilities cancel in a(x)); dina.R:629 (helper header states a per-arm contract); roxygen dina.R:95-98
fix_summary: Either make the 'unknown' branch produce arm-specific probabilities as the helper's stated contract says, or document that the option is currently equivalent to no censoring adjustment; which of the two is the author's method decision.

summary: dina() and dina_bagged() document `df` as 'data frame (or tibble / data.table)', but the shared extraction helper selects columns with `df[, required_cols]`, which in this data.table-importing namespace is evaluated with data.table semantics and stops for every data.table input. Also at: dina_df.R:256 (same idiom; not reached for a data.table because 244 stops first); dina_subgroup.R:669 and dina_subgroup.R:674 (.dina_extract_X_from_df, called at dina_subgroup.R:408, dina_subgroup.R:1228, dina_subgroup_bootstrap.R:635); dina_df.R:35-36 (the roxygen claim; inherited by dina_bagged via @inheritParams at dina_df.R:129; rendered man/dina.Rd:18, man/dina_bagged.Rd:18); package call sites that pass the caller's frame straight through: forestsearch_helpers.R:1534 (subgroup_method = "dina", no tryCatch), forestsearch_main.R:3206 (use_dina = TRUE, inside a tryCatch that turns the error into the warning 'DINA analysis failed')
fix_summary: Coerce `df` to a plain data frame at the top of both extraction helpers so the documented tibble / data.table inputs work (or, alternatively, drop the data.table claim from the dina() roxygen and reject data.table input with the package's own message).

summary: dina_subgroup() and dina_frontier() check only that the fit has length(covariates) + 1 coefficients and then pair coefficients with columns by position, so a `covariates` vector in a different order (or naming different columns) than the fit was trained on silently gives a wrong tau-hat and a wrong subgroup. Also at: dina_subgroup.R:435 (positional tau_hat); dina_subgroup.R:1236 and dina_subgroup.R:1240 (same length-only check and positional product in dina_frontier); reachable from forestsearch() only through a user-supplied dina_res: forestsearch_helpers.R:1529 and forestsearch_main.R:3197
fix_summary: Compare names(coef(fit))[-1] with `covariates` in both functions and stop (or reorder by name) on a mismatch.

summary: The returned `labels`/`label` render the threshold with paste0() on the raw double (15 significant digits), so evaluating the documented label with get_dfpred() can drop the observations sitting exactly on the threshold and disagree with the returned `mask` and `n_subgroup`. Also at: dina_subgroup.R:584-587 (`label`, same rendering); dina_subgroup.R:249-251 (roxygen: labels are 'in the form consumed by get_dfpred()'); forestsearch_helpers.R:1661-1662 (forestsearch path re-renders with 17 significant digits and does not use sg$labels)
fix_summary: Render the threshold in labels/label with a round-trip format (17 significant digits), as .forestsearch_dina_select() already does.

summary: The depth-1 enumeration includes the non-cuts `x <= max(x)` and `x >= min(x)` (the whole sample, empty complement) for every covariate, so dina_subgroup() can return the entire data set as the selected 'subgroup' and dina_frontier() carries full-sample 'cuts' on every wide frontier. Also at: dina_subgroup.R:743-749 (admitted on size and floor only); dina_subgroup.R:536 (maxSG ranks size first); dina_subgroup.R:835-838 (depth-2 grid uses all unique values, including min/max, for low-cardinality covariates, giving conjunctions that duplicate a singleton); dina_subgroup.R:1282-1284 (per-covariate frontier keeps the full-sample cuts)
fix_summary: Decide explicitly how a candidate whose mask covers the whole sample (empty complement) is to be treated by the collectors; at present it is admitted without any check or flag.

summary: The harm orientation (tau_sign) that forestsearch applies to DINA for continuous/binary outcomes with adverse_outcome = FALSE exists only on the subgroup_method = "dina" path: dina_frontier() has no such argument and the use_dina screening call to dina_subgroup() omits it, so on those outcomes the DINA screening cuts are ranked and floored in the opposite (benefit) direction, contrary to the documented 'same cut subgroup_method = "dina" would select'. Also at: dina_subgroup.R:1240 (tau_hat without orientation); forestsearch_main.R:3217 (use_dina screening calls dina_frontier with da$frontier only); forestsearch_main.R:3239 (use_dina selected_only screening calls dina_subgroup() WITHOUT tau_sign); forestsearch_main.R:434-438 (roxygen: screening contributes 'the same cut subgroup_method = "dina" would select'); forestsearch_helpers.R:1561 (details-time frontier display, un-oriented); forestsearch_main.R:3239
fix_summary: Give dina_frontier() the same tau_sign orientation as dina_subgroup() and pass .dina_tau_sign() from all forestsearch call sites, including the use_dina screening call to dina_subgroup().

summary: The exported get_dfpred() called with sg.harm = NULL or character(0), which is what a no-subgroup fit carries, silently flags every row as a harm-subgroup member (treat.recommend = 0) instead of raising an error or returning nobody. Also at: forestsearch_helpers.R:137
fix_summary: Reject a NULL or zero-length sg.harm with an informative error (or return an all-complement flag) instead of the vacuous all-member result.

summary: evaluate_comparison() coerces numeric-level factors but not numeric-valued character columns, so a cut label on such a column is compared as strings, unlike the DINA and GRF coding that selected the cut on the numeric values and whose comments say the coercion is the same. Also at: forestsearch_helpers.R:1344-1347, 1373-1374, 1510-1512 (roxygen / comments stating the coercion is identical to evaluate_comparison())
fix_summary: Apply the same all-numeric coercion to character columns as to factors in evaluate_comparison(), so the label evaluator matches the DINA / GRF coding.

summary: Effect-based re-selection overwrites only some winner fields, so the stored identifier object (grp.consistency$out_sg / fs$grf_res) mixes the new winner's definition with the native winner's label, SE, CI (DINA) or sg.harm.id, data$treat.recommend, grf.gsub, selected_depth/best_depth, cate_sg (GRF). Also at: forestsearch_helpers.R:1793-1794 (.grf_reselect_on_effect replaces only sg_def); forestsearch_helpers.R:1953-1957 (.forestsearch_grf_select details line prints the native winner's depth)
fix_summary: After re-selection, recompute or clear every winner-specific field of the stored identifier object (DINA: labels, label, se_mean_tau_hat, ci; GRF: sg.harm.id, data$treat.recommend, grf.gsub, selected_depth/best_depth, cate_sg).

summary: For count outcomes forestsearch() requires offset.name for IRR, but the DINA fit is called without exposure and dina()/dina_fit() have no offset argument, so DINA's tau-hat and the m_diff = log(threshold) proposal floor are on the mean-count ratio while forestsearch's text calls that floor log(IRR). Also at: forestsearch_main.R:3200-3206 (use_dina screening fit, same call shape); dina_df.R:84-90 and dina.R:157-167 (no offset/exposure formal); dina.R:537-544 and 842-845 (Poisson fits of the raw count); forestsearch_main.R:444-445 and dina_subgroup.R:403 (text calling the Poisson tau-hat log(IRR))
fix_summary: Either carry the exposure offset through dina()/dina_fit() for the Poisson family, or state in the documentation and at run time that DINA's proposal ignores offset.name and correct the 'log(IRR)' wording.

summary: When effect-based re-selection scores no candidate or errors, the native-statistic winner is returned silently with no effect floor applied; this happens deterministically for subgroup_method = "grf" with effect_measure = "IRD", because the per-candidate estimator returns NULL for IRD. Also at: forestsearch_helpers.R:1252 (DINA nothing-scorable return); forestsearch_helpers.R:1620 and 1924 (error = function(e) sg / grf_res); forestsearch_helpers.R:1774-1779 (frontier-selector error converted to 'admitted set empty')
fix_summary: Raise a warning (an error under mr_inference) when re-selection fails or scores no candidate, record on the result which statistic actually selected, and refuse or handle estimands the per-candidate scorer cannot represent (IRD) instead of falling back.

summary: forestsearch() documents est.scale as "hr" or "rmst", never reads or validates it, and no code implements "rmst" (every consumer of the stored value knows only "hr" and "1/hr"), so the documented "rmst" is silently treated as "hr" by the search, tables and cross-validation and makes the full bootstrap run all replicates and then return no estimates. Also at: forestsearch_main.R:1637 (formal est.scale = "hr", never read in the body), 1880-1881 (captured unvalidated into args_call_all); man/forestsearch.Rd:150; bootstrap_dofuture_main.R:267, 559, 568, 574-616, 618-639; bootstrap_calculations_helpers.R:278-279 (get_dfRes), 162-163 (ci_est); summary_utility_functions.R:52, 1157 and forestsearch_cross_validation.R:574 (any value other than "1/hr" is treated as "hr")
fix_summary: Correct the @param to the values the code supports ("hr", "1/hr") and validate est.scale at entry to forestsearch() so any other value fails before the search.

summary: violated: roxygen states a default that the formal (or the code's effective default) contradicts at 12 confirmed sites in 11 functions, headed by forestsearch(use_twostage) documented FALSE with formal TRUE; three nested list-element defaults and one cross-reference are also wrong, and no reader claim was refuted at source. Also at: Cox_estimation_helpers.R:8; calibrate_glm_interaction.R:48; truefind_asymptotic_glm.R:180; cox_spline_fit.R:537; dina_subgroup.R:168; fpr_approximation.R:57; gg_forest.R:92; simulation_tables.R:1043; bootstrap_analysis_dofuture.R:78; forestsearch_main.R:1001; forestsearch_main.R:978; subgroup_consistency_main.R:276; run_subgroup_sims.R:200; forestsearch_main.R:928; forestsearch_main.R:1700; Cox_estimation_helpers.R:8; bootstrap_analysis_dofuture.R:79; calibrate_glm_interaction.R:48; cox_spline_fit.R:536; dina_subgroup.R:168; forestsearch_main.R:1001; fpr_approximation.R:56; simulation_tables.R:1043; fpr_approximation.R:57
fix_summary: Correct the roxygen text at each listed site to the formal or effective default (or, where the documented value was the intended one, decide per site whether the formal should change instead).

summary: The documented tune_grf argument of forestsearch() is never read in the function body or forwarded to any GRF fit, so tune_grf = TRUE silently changes nothing on both the use_grf screening path and the subgroup_method = "grf" path. Also at: forestsearch_main.R:1077-1083 (roxygen claim), 3078-3092 and 3095-3112 (use_grf call sites), 2945-2965 (subgroup_method = "grf"); grf_args.R:25-44, 86-102 (builders have no tune_grf formal); forestsearch_helpers.R:1833-1851 (.forestsearch_grf_select has none); forestsearch_main.R:1711
fix_summary: Forward tune_grf through the two GRF argument builders and .forestsearch_grf_select() to the GRF fits, or remove the formal and its documentation.

summary: The overdispersion argument is forwarded only to the GRF routines and never reaches the effect estimator, so on the default subgroup_method = "consistency" path with a count outcome and use_grf = FALSE, "quasi" and "negbin" change nothing. Also at: forestsearch_main.R:1709 (formal), 1067-1071 (roxygen), 2704-2711 (PS rebuild, also without it), 2952 and 3110 (the only consumers: GRF paths); glm_effect_estimators.R:100-112 (no overdispersion formal), 198-213 and 783, 811, 870 (always stats::poisson)
fix_summary: Either carry overdispersion into the count effect estimator or document (and warn) that it applies to the GRF paths only.

summary: A user-supplied effect or consistency threshold above 1 is replaced by the package default for effect_measure = "IRD" as well as "RD" on the ground that both are bounded in [-1, 1], which is not true of an incidence-rate difference, and the warning names 0.05 as the applied value when 0.01 is applied for IRD. Also at: forestsearch_main.R:296-310 (validation warning 'A risk difference cannot exceed 1.0' for IRD), 2303 (message hard-codes 0.05 while 2305-2306 applies 0.01 for IRD), 2312-2324 (consistency threshold > 1 reset to 0.0), 1271-1273 (roxygen: a supplied value is used as given)
fix_summary: Restrict the greater-than-1 remap to RD, leave supplied IRD thresholds as given, and make the warning report the value actually applied.

summary: A user-supplied ps_hat is silently discarded, unvalidated, whenever ps_method resolves to "none", which is the default for is.RCT = TRUE, so a call supplying propensity scores with ps_adjust_method = "iptw" runs unadjusted with no message. Also at: forestsearch_main.R:2596-2599 (ps_method resolves to "none" for is.RCT = TRUE), 2639-2641 (ps_adjust_method forced to "none"), 1131-1142 (ps_hat roxygen)
fix_summary: Warn or stop when ps_hat is supplied (or ps_adjust_method is not "none") while ps_method resolves to "none".

summary: When ps_method resolves to anything other than "none" on a GLM outcome, the estimator closure is rebuilt without adverse_outcome and reverts to make_effect_estimator()'s default TRUE, so the candidate search screens and ranks on the un-flipped outcome whenever the resolved adverse_outcome is FALSE (the continuous default, or binary with adverse_outcome = FALSE). Also at: forestsearch_main.R:2227 (first build passes adverse_outcome), forestsearch_main.R:3623 and :3841 (resample-consistency spec and MR spec carry the resolved adverse_outcome), glm_effect_estimators.R:107 (formal default adverse_outcome = TRUE)
fix_summary: Pass the resolved adverse_outcome to the propensity-branch rebuild of the estimator closure so it matches the first construction.

summary: On the subgroup_method = "dina" and "grf" branches mr_harm_confirmed is isTRUE(harm_flag), so an MR result whose harm_flag is NA (selected subgroup could not be fitted) is reported as FALSE, whereas the consistency branch and the documentation return NA for that case. Also at: forestsearch_main.R:3060-3061 (GRF branch, same expression); contrast forestsearch_main.R:3956-3957 (consistency branch keeps NA); forestsearch_main.R:3919-3927 (no .mr_skip message for the short variant on any branch); roxygen forestsearch_main.R:1225-1233, 1380-1389
fix_summary: Return harm_flag unchanged on the DINA and GRF branches as the consistency branch does, and route the short variant through the existing not-performed message on all three branches.

summary: With use_grf = TRUE a supplied grf_res that already has tree.cuts is never read for its cuts (no GRF cut enters the candidate family, with no message), and a supplied grf_cuts without grf_res is overwritten by a fresh GRF fit, so the documented reuse works only when both are supplied together. Also at: forestsearch_main.R:3124 and :3164 (user-supplied grf_cuts overwritten after a refit); forestsearch_main.R:3316 (grf_cuts passed on); get_fsdata.R:252 (use_grf switched off silently when grf_cuts is NULL); roxygen forestsearch_main.R:389-400
fix_summary: Take grf_cuts from a supplied grf_res when grf_cuts is NULL, and skip the refit when grf_cuts is supplied.

summary: df.analysis is never coerced to a base data.frame, and Y, Event, Treat, id and the dummy matrix are built with df[, name], which does not drop to a vector for a tibble (and is not column selection by a character variable for a data.table), so such inputs are expected to fail with an internal error or a 'no subgroup' early return instead of being coerced or rejected at entry. Also at: forestsearch_main.R:3352, :3358, :3390 (single-column `[` relied on to drop to a vector); :3386-3387 with get_FSdata_helpers.R:747 (as.factor(df[, i])); :3391 (data.frame(Y, Event, Treat, id, ...)); get_fsdata.R:99-106 and forestsearch_main.R:1920 (is.data.frame() guards let tibble / data.table through although the message tells users to coerce them); get_fsdata.R:99
fix_summary: Coerce df.analysis (and df.predict / df.test) to a base data.frame at entry, or reject non-base classes there with the message get_FSdata() already carries.

summary: With propensity adjustment requested on a GLM outcome (ps_method not "none" and ps_adjust_method "iptw" or "dr_gcomp") the weights are used only in the candidate search: the consistency frame df.fs is built without sw / ips_covar / ps_hat, so the consistency stage (split and resample) and MR silently fit unadjusted models, and the documented automatic fallback to "split" for propensity-adjusted effects does not exist. Also at: forestsearch_main.R:3398-3409 (only outcome / treat / offset re-attached to df.fs); :3616-3625 (glm_resample_spec has no PS field); :3837-3841 (MR spec has no PS field); roxygen :1042-1044 and NEWS.md:1490-1495 (claim propensity-adjusted effects fall back to "split"); glm_effect_estimators.R:322, 465, 579, 592, 776, 802, 956 (guards that drop the adjustment when the column is absent); subgroup_consistency_main.R:428-437; consistency_resample.R:203-221; subgroup_consistency_helpers.R:343; forestsearch_main.R:1042
fix_summary: Carry the propensity columns onto df.fs and either route propensity-adjusted fits to a consistency/MR path that uses them or refuse the combination, and correct the fallback claim in the roxygen.

summary: On GLM outcomes the user's outcome/treatment/offset column is attached to the consistency frame only if its name is not already taken, so a GLM outcome column literally named "Event" is silently replaced by the all-ones placeholder and the consistency stage (and GLM MR) evaluate a constant outcome while the search scored the real one. Also at: forestsearch_main.R:3356 (GLM placeholder Event <- rep(1L, ...)), :3391 (df.fs built with internal Y/Event/Treat/id), :3402, :3405-3407 (same not-already-present guard for treat.name and offset.name), :3419-3425 (reserved-name stop exists for adjust_covariates only), :3620 and :3838 (outcome.name handed to the consistency resample spec and to the GLM MR spec, both evaluated on df.fs)
fix_summary: Stop (as is already done for adjust_covariates) when outcome.name, treat.name or offset.name names a different internal column of the consistency frame, or build that frame without reusing user-visible names.

summary: Under sg_focus = "maxeff" (documented as the effect argmax with no effect or consistency threshold, and recorded with an unrestricted admission set) the consistency-stage entry gate still requires some candidate effect to exceed c2, so when the largest candidate effect is <= c2 the stage is skipped and no subgroup is returned instead of the argmax. Also at: forestsearch_main.R:3540-3544 (check_threshold), forestsearch_main.R:3552 and :3745 (stage skipped, no else branch), forestsearch_main.R:134-135 (c2 derived as 0.80 * c1 for every focus, so hr.threshold alone moves the gate under maxeff), fs_to_guohe.R:145-147 (the maxeff bridge stops with 'No maxeff candidate family' on a gate-failed fit)
fix_summary: Either make the Section 8 gate read the resolved admission decision (.admit_applies) so the c2 comparison is not applied when no floor applies, or keep the gate and state it in the maxeff documentation, the override warning and the recorded admission set.

summary: forestsearch() never passes its seedit to subgroup.consistency(seed = ), so the random consistency splits are always seeded with the callee's own default 8316951 and changing seedit has no effect on them. Also at: forestsearch_main.R:3629-3633 (filter_call_args call), :381 (roxygen 'Random seed'), :1636 (formal seedit); subgroup_consistency_main.R:397 (formal seed = 8316951), :497-499 (set.seed(seed)), :970-971 (per-candidate streams); summary_utility_functions.R:679-688 (filter_call_args)
fix_summary: Pass seedit as the seed of the subgroup.consistency() call (or document that the split seed is fixed and independent of seedit).

summary: merge() is called with its default sort = TRUE, so on the consistency path df.est and df.predict come back ordered by the id key while grp.consistency$sg.harm.id and df_flag stay in input row order, and positional consumers misalign whenever df.analysis is not already in ascending id order. Also at: forestsearch_main.R:3733; positional consumers: fs_to_guohe.R:159 with :232-248 (fs_assert_membership, run by default from fs_to_guohe.R:343), plot_km_band_forestsearch.R:729-733 ('Assume same row order', reached when id.name != "id"); order-preserving siblings: forestsearch_helpers.R:1665, 1988; plot_km_band_forestsearch.R:731
fix_summary: Attach the flag positionally (or merge with sort = FALSE and restore input order) so df.est and df.predict rows stay aligned with df.analysis and sg.harm.id on every path.

summary: On the survival MR path adjust_covariates is intersected with the column names of the scoring frame, so any adjustment term that is not a bare column name (the documented "strata(x1)", or pspline()) is silently dropped and MR is computed from an unadjusted or partially adjusted Cox model while search and consistency used the adjusted one. Also at: fs_mr_inference_methods.R:207-208 (.fs_mr_spec: the same intersect() for the DINA and GRF MR branches, called at forestsearch_main.R:2845 and :3033); forestsearch_main.R:1088-1094 (roxygen documenting "strata(x1)")
fix_summary: Pass the adjustment terms to the MR spec exactly as the identifier used them (checking the underlying variables rather than the term strings), or stop/skip MR with a message when a term cannot be honoured.

summary: On the consistency branch (the default subgroup_method) forestsearch() calls fs_mr_inference() without field_R_out / field_R_in, so those two mr_inference_args entries are silently ignored and the field block always runs at 1000 x 500 outer/inner draws. Also at: fs_mr_inference.R:597-598 (formal defaults 1000L / 500L), :919-920, :947, :985 (use and echo); fs_mr_inference_methods.R:178-179 (sibling DINA/GRF wrapper that does forward them); mr_method_tables.R:55 (roxygen example passing them through forestsearch()); tests/testthat/test-mr-method-tables.R:121; forestsearch_main.R:3844
fix_summary: Forward mr_inference_args$field_R_out and $field_R_in in the consistency-branch call (ideally by routing that branch through the same wrapper as DINA/GRF so the forwarded sets cannot diverge).

summary: .fs_apply_mr() forwards 25 of fs_mr_inference()'s 29 arguments and drops keep_declaration_field, keep_field_matrix, declaration_c0 and pconsistency.digits, so on the DINA and GRF branches those mr_inference_args entries are silently ignored although the roxygen and NEWS say the full set is forwarded. Also at: fs_mr_inference_methods.R:120 (roxygen: 'forwards the full fs_mr_inference() argument set'); NEWS.md:584-594 (same claim); forestsearch_main.R:2860, :3045 (DINA / GRF call sites); forestsearch_main.R:3905-3911 (consistency branch forwards all four); fs_mr_inference_methods.R:157
fix_summary: Forward the four remaining arguments from mr_inference_args (and pconsistency.digits from the caller), or state in the roxygen/NEWS that the declaration-field arguments are not supported on the DINA and GRF branches.

summary: For binary, continuous and count outcomes lasso_selection() returns "(Intercept)" in `selected`, so get_FSdata()'s 'if any selected' guard is always true and, when LASSO keeps no covariate, every confounder is filtered out (error / NULL fit) whereas the survival path keeps the whole pool. Also at: get_fsdata.R:354 (guard that the intercept defeats); forestsearch_main.R:3342-3344 (count includes the intercept and is labelled 'Cox-LASSO' for every outcome type)
fix_summary: Drop the intercept from the selected/omitted sets returned by lasso_selection() and apply one empty-selection rule to all outcome types.

summary: A factor confounder with at least cont.cutoff (default 4) observed values and numeric-parsable levels makes get_FSdata() stop under the default collapse_cuts = TRUE, because collapse_redundant_cuts() calls stats::sd() on the raw factor column, so forestsearch() returns its early-exit list (sg.harm = NULL, error_log stage 'get_FSdata') with a base-R message about var() on a factor. Also at: get_FSdata_helpers.R:703-705 (membership safety check applies <= / >= to the raw factor; unreachable today because sd() stops first, but it would give NA and zero flips if only sd() were patched); get_fsdata.R:480 (median() on the raw factor under cut_type = "median" or when the factor is named in conf.cont_medians / conf.cont_medians_force; independent of collapse_cuts)
fix_summary: Coerce numeric-level factor columns to their numeric values (as process_conf_force_expr() and evaluate_comparison() already do) before sd(), the membership comparisons of the safety check and the median computation, or reject such columns at entry with a clear message.

summary: Missing confounder values are counted as a distinct level both when a variable is classed continuous and when a cut is tested for having more than one level, so a cut that is constant on every observed row is kept and returned as a one-level candidate factor. Also at: get_FSdata_helpers.R:11
fix_summary: Count distinct non-missing values in both tests and decide explicitly at entry (error, or a documented rule) how missing confounder values are handled.

summary: Supplying conf.cont_medians or conf.cont_medians_force silently removes every cut on all other continuous confounders, and under the default cut_type the variables named in conf.cont_medians receive the four default cuts instead of a median cut, both contrary to the roxygen. Also at: get_fsdata.R:399-414; get_fsdata.R:31-32; forestsearch_main.R:581-588
fix_summary: Make the code and the documentation agree on whether these arguments add median cuts to the default grid or restrict which continuous confounders are cut, and state the chosen rule in the roxygen of both functions.

summary: Every confounder with fewer than cont.cutoff (default 4) unique values enters the candidate pool as its bare name, which is evaluated as `x == 1` with no check that the variable is a 0/1 indicator, so a categorical confounder with no level equal to 1 (factor F/M, numeric 0/2) is removed from the search with no warning and a 3-level one contributes only 'level 1 versus the rest' under a label that reads as a binary indicator. Also at: get_fsdata.R:185-195 (type check accepts any numeric or factor); get_fsdata.R:272-279,286-287 (fewer than cont.cutoff unique values -> categorical, bare name); get_fsdata.R:499 (GRF cut on the same variable discarded by substring match against the bare name); get_fsdata.R:618,634,636-638,641 (evaluation, drop, details-gated cat); get_FSdata_helpers.R:856,859 (is_valid); forestsearch_helpers.R:224-227 (bare name evaluated as == 1); forestsearch_main.R:3318 (details = FALSE hard-coded in the get_FSdata call); forestsearch_main.R:3363-3366 (only the surviving candidate list is printed under details = TRUE)
fix_summary: Where categorical confounders enter the pool, either expand each one to one indicator per level or stop (or warn unconditionally) when a categorical confounder is not a 0/1 indicator, and state the rule in the confounders.name documentation and in the methodology article.

summary: Existing candidates are compared with GRF and DINA cuts by unanchored grepl() regex matching, so a GRF or DINA cut is discarded as already represented whenever any categorical confounder name (or median-cut string) is merely a substring of it. Also at: get_fsdata.R:520; get_fsdata.R:451
fix_summary: Compare on the parsed variable name (and operator and value where a full-expression match is intended) with exact or word-anchored matching instead of substring regex.

summary: Caller-supplied dina_cuts enter the candidate pool whenever non-empty, with no use_dina gate, unlike grf_cuts (inert unless use_grf = TRUE), while the family status, the family enumerators and the bootstrap/CV replays all treat the run as having no DINA cuts. Also at: forestsearch_main.R:3317
fix_summary: Either gate the DINA merge on use_dina the way the GRF merge is gated on use_grf, or document that dina_cuts alone activates them and make the family status, enumerators and replays carry the supplied cuts consistently.

summary: conf_force expressions are not validated: one whose right-hand side is not a number (compound expression, unsupported function, typo) is compared as a character string and silently becomes a mislabelled candidate or is silently dropped. Also at: forestsearch_helpers.R:207-208; get_FSdata_helpers.R:414-417; get_FSdata_helpers.R:435-438
fix_summary: Validate each conf_force element as a single 'variable operator number' comparison (or a supported deferred form) and stop on anything else, and refuse ordered comparisons whose right-hand side is not numeric.

summary: exclude_cuts is applied only before collapse_redundant_cuts(), so the default coarsening (collapse_cuts = TRUE, digits = 0) can rewrite a surviving cut into exactly the excluded expression, which is then returned and searched. Also at: get_fsdata.R:550-572; get_FSdata_helpers.R:702-713
fix_summary: Re-apply the exclude_cuts filter after the coarsening step (keeping the existing first pass so excluded thresholds do not enter cluster centroids).

summary: Cuts that evaluate to a single value are dropped silently (the only message is under details = TRUE, which forestsearch() hard-codes to FALSE) and the zero-candidate diagnostic is tested only before that filter, so get_FSdata() can return an empty candidate set and forestsearch() then stops in dummy() with an unrelated message. Also at: get_fsdata.R:574; get_fsdata.R:648; get_FSdata_helpers.R:428-434; forestsearch_main.R:3318; forestsearch_main.R:3386-3387; get_FSdata_helpers.R:776
fix_summary: Repeat the zero-candidate diagnostic after the validity filter and emit a warning (independent of details) naming the cuts or confounders dropped for having one level.

summary: Candidate factor columns are written as q1, q2, ... with no collision check, so an input column carrying one of those names (for example a covariate called q1) is silently overwritten by a 0/1 factor in the returned data frame. Also at: get_fsdata.R:666-667; get_fsdata.R:685; get_fsdata.R:700; get_fsdata.R:708; bootstrap_analysis_dofuture.R:393-396
fix_summary: Stop with a clear message when a generated factor name collides with a column named in confounders.name or the outcome/event columns (or generate names that cannot collide).

summary: For a binary outcome with a rate measure (IRR) and adverse_outcome = FALSE, the search estimator fits the rate ratio of Y (the flag is not forwarded to the Poisson rate estimator) while the default resample consistency fit flips Y to 1 - Y first, so the consistency rate describes a different quantity from the one the search ranked. Also at: consistency_resample.R:255-260; forestsearch_main.R:3616-3624
fix_summary: Apply one convention on both sides for binary rate measures: either reject adverse_outcome = FALSE with IRR/IRD or make the resample fit skip the flip exactly where the estimator does.

summary: effect_measure is validated against the outcome type for binary and count outcomes but not for continuous, so a ratio or risk measure supplied with outcome_type = 'continuous' is accepted: the estimate is a mean difference while forestsearch() log-transforms the thresholds, labels the effect with the supplied measure and exponentiates it for display. Also at: forestsearch_main.R:1789-1795; forestsearch_main.R:2340-2368; forestsearch_main.R:3607-3609; forestsearch_main.R:3616-3625; forestsearch_main.R:1789
fix_summary: Validate effect_measure in the continuous branch (only 'MD') and stop on a mismatch, in make_effect_estimator() and at forestsearch() entry.

summary: A requested ps_adjust_method has no implementation for several measure/method pairs (RR with iptw or dr_gcomp, RD with dr_gcomp, MD with dr_gcomp), yet forestsearch() accepts every method for every GLM measure, fits those cases unadjusted and still reports the requested method; the literal-split consistency fits and the bootstrap/table estimators are also unadjusted because their data or closure carry no propensity columns. Also at: glm_effect_estimators.R:414-419; glm_effect_estimators.R:465; glm_effect_estimators.R:952-966; forestsearch_main.R:2639-2641; forestsearch_main.R:2705-2712; forestsearch_main.R:3391-3409; subgroup_consistency_helpers.R:300-301; bootstrap_dofuture_main.R:302-310; summary_utility_functions.R:983-990; mr_estimates_table.R:204-208
fix_summary: Reject at forestsearch() entry (or in the factory) a ps_adjust_method that has no implementation for the resolved effect measure, and either carry the propensity columns onto the consistency frame or state that split consistency is unadjusted.

summary: With effect_measure = "RD" and no covariates, a slice with an arm at 0% or 100% events gets its standard error from the logistic tier as (logit treatment-coefficient SE) x mean(p1(1-p1)), which is near zero when the treated arm is degenerate and in the hundreds to thousands when the control arm is, while the point estimate is correct and converged = TRUE is returned. Also at: glm_effect_estimators.R:536 (se_rd), :541 (converged = TRUE), :545 (method_used), :548 (error-only handler, so tier 3 at :553-556 is skipped); consumers of the SE: subgroup_search.R:1079-1081 (candidate-table Wald limits), Cox_estimation_helpers.R:224 -> bootstrap_dofuture_main.R:336-338 -> :577/:599 -> bootstrap_calculations_helpers.R:286 (unadjusted CI), summary_utility_functions.R:219-225 (displayed CI)
fix_summary: On unadjusted slices with a degenerate arm, return a standard error that is valid at the boundary (the raw-proportion form already written in tier 3) instead of accepting the quasi-separated logistic fit in tier 2.

summary: With the non-default effect_measure = "RR", the log-binomial attempt in .estimate_rr() handles warnings in an exiting tryCatch() handler that calls invokeRestart("muffleWarning"), so a glm "step size truncated" warning becomes the uncaught error "no 'restart' 'muffleWarning' found" and the modified-Poisson fallback at :680-705 is never reached. Also at: glm_effect_estimators.R:505-510 (.estimate_rd tier 1, identical handler; suspected only: the unadjusted RD fit cannot warn because its start value is already the MLE, so this site needs adjust_covariates, which the roxygen at :63-68 marks as implemented but untested)
fix_summary: Handle non-"converge" warnings from the log-binomial attempt (and the identity-link tier in .estimate_rd) without invoking a restart from an exiting handler, either by muffling them in a calling handler or by routing them to the next fallback tier.

summary: The IPTW branch of the Poisson rate estimator never looks at effect_measure, so with effect_measure = "IRD" and ps_adjust_method = "iptw" it returns the log incidence rate ratio while every caller treats the value as a rate difference. Also at: glm_effect_estimators.R:786-794 (returns coefficient, measure = "log-IRR"); glm_effect_estimators.R:749 (IRR existence check skipped because effect_measure is IRD); forestsearch_main.R:2705-2712 (closure rebuilt with ps_adjust_method); subgroup_search.R:680 (consumer)
fix_summary: Make the IPTW branch honour effect_measure = "IRD" (compute the weighted rate difference as the other branches do) or reject the IRD + iptw combination with an error.

summary: .grf_code_column() derives the coding of a character column from the values present in the frame it is handed (unique(x), NA included), so a GRF cut can be evaluated on a different numeric scale on the unfiltered df, df.predict or df.test than the scale the forest split on. Also at: grf_helpers.R:690 (codes from the values present); grf_subgroup_labels.R:225 (evaluator); forestsearch_helpers.R:1987, 1990, 1993 (evaluator applied to df, df.predict, df.test); forestsearch_helpers.R:1369 (.coerce_covariates_numeric has the same unique(col)-with-NA test)
fix_summary: Derive the coding from a level set fixed at fit time and carried with the subgroup definition, and ignore NA when testing whether the labels are all numeric.

summary: The survival GRF path builds its covariate matrix with apply(data[, confounders], 2, as.numeric), which passes through a character matrix whenever any confounder is a factor or character: non-numeric labels become NA, numeric columns are rounded to 7 significant digits, and the coding differs from the GLM path and from the subgroup evaluator. Also at: grf_main.R:308 and forestsearch_helpers.R:1987 (membership re-derived on the raw columns); grf_helpers.R:427-436 (tree-path membership from predict(tree, X)); grf_subg_harm_glm.R:868-894 (sibling .build_grf_X coding)
fix_summary: Build the survival covariate matrix with the same per-column coding the GLM path and the evaluator use (.build_grf_X / .grf_code_column).

summary: When validate_grf_data() rejects the data (one treatment level, one event level such as fully uncensored data, or an arm smaller than n.min), the early exit calls create_null_result() with trees = list(), which stops with 'subscript out of bounds' instead of returning the null result. Also at: grf_helpers.R:535 (trees[[1]] on an empty list), grf_helpers.R:536, grf_helpers.R:559; grf_helpers.R:535
fix_summary: Pass NULL (as the frontier no-selection exit does) or make create_null_result() tolerate an empty tree list so the early exit returns the null result.

summary: Both GRF identifiers test the frontier selection with is.null() only, but .grf_frontier_select() returns a zero-row data frame when the band is empty (effMaxSG/effMinSG with a negative maximum eligible effect), and the next step stops with 'argument is of length zero'. Also at: grf_subg_harm_glm.R:528 and 547 (same is.null-only test); grf_subgroup_labels.R:387-391 (zero-row return), grf_subgroup_labels.R:405 (where it stops)
fix_summary: Treat a zero-row selection as no subgroup in both identifiers, as .grf_reselect_on_effect() already does.

summary: When no DR candidate clears dmin.grf, the frontier no-selection return omits the candidates table, so the effect-based re-selection (default grf_select_statistic = 'effect') is skipped and dmin.grf acts as an all-or-nothing gate on the DR scale, although it is not applied to individual candidates once any one clears it. Also at: grf_subg_harm_glm.R:532-545 (same omission on the GLM identifier); forestsearch_helpers.R:1910-1913 (consumer that skips the re-selection); forestsearch_helpers.R:1913
fix_summary: Either attach the candidate family to the frontier no-selection returns of both identifiers so the effect floor is the only admission rule, or document that dmin.grf is applied first as an existence gate on the DR scale.

summary: return_selected_cuts_only is accepted by grf.subg.harm.glm() but never acted on (cuts always come from the single best-depth tree), and frac.tau and conf.level there, and id.name in grf.subg.harm.survival(), are likewise accepted and unused. Also at: grf_subg_harm_glm.R:297 (frac.tau), 301 (conf.level), 900 (n and n.min unused in .select_best_sg_glm); grf_main.R:155 (id.name unused); grf_helpers.R:35-36 (config fields nothing reads)
fix_summary: Honour return_selected_cuts_only on the GLM identifier as the survival one does, or document it as having no effect there, and remove or document the other unused arguments.

summary: For outcome_type = "count" the adverse_outcome orientation is never applied to the GRF outcome, so the GRF 'harm' subgroup is the region where treatment LOWERS the count, the opposite of the documented meaning of adverse_outcome = TRUE and of the package's own count convention (IRR > 1 = harm). Also at: grf_subg_harm_glm.R:451 (comment 'flip not needed'); grf_subg_harm_glm.R:100-103 (roxygen: adverse event count => harm = treatment increases outcome); grf_subg_harm_glm.R:519-528 (frontier branch: same unflipped scores, native gate); grf_subgroup_labels.R:274,307,361 (candidate effect = control - treated; eligibility effect >= dmin); forestsearch_helpers.R:1910-1913,1937-1939 (consumer; re-ranking skipped when $candidates is absent); forestsearch_main.R:1797-1798, 2198-2199 (adverse_outcome resolves TRUE for count); run_simulation_analysis.R:1248-1250 (standalone GRF arm)
fix_summary: Orient the count GRF outcome so that a higher count is the worse outcome when adverse_outcome is TRUE (as already done for binary and continuous), and correct the comment at line 451.

summary: With sg.criterion = 'Nsg' the GLM selector returns the largest subgroup without comparing its score with dmin.grf, whereas the 'mDiff' branch and the survival sibling both apply the threshold.
fix_summary: Apply the dmin.grf threshold in the 'Nsg' branch as select_best_subgroup() does.

summary: consistency_threshold = NULL is documented as falling back to hr.consistency, but on the split path it is never resolved: with estimator_fn supplied and the threshold NULL the splitter skips the GLM estimator and runs the survival branch, so a direct GLM caller silently gets no subgroup (or a Cox comparison if the frame happens to carry Y/Event/Treat). Also at: subgroup_consistency_main.R:209-210 (roxygen: "Default NULL (uses hr.consistency)"); subgroup_consistency_helpers.R:241-242 (same statement for run_single_consistency_split); subgroup_consistency_helpers.R:288 (GLM branch needs both estimator_fn and a non-NULL consistency_threshold); subgroup_consistency_helpers.R:1744 (two-stage copy of the same condition); subgroup_consistency_helpers.R:241
fix_summary: Resolve a NULL consistency_threshold to hr.consistency when estimator_fn is supplied (as the roxygen states), or make the GLM branch depend on estimator_fn alone.

summary: Under sg_focus = "maxeff" a finite m1.threshold is accepted and silently not applied, because the branch that skips the effect floor also skips the m1 filter, and neither the maxeff override warning nor the documentation nor fs_family_report() says so. Also at: forestsearch_main.R:2017-2041 (maxeff override block: m1.threshold neither reset nor named in the warning); forestsearch_main.R:699-701 (maxeff roxygen lists what is disabled, m1.threshold not among them); fs_family_report.R:170-175 and :327-329 (m1 filter reported as data-dependent/active under maxeff; note also cites stale lines "L516-531" and calls m1 a treatment-arm count, whereas it is the treatment-arm median, subgroup_search.R:1204 / forestsearch_main.R:849)
fix_summary: Have forestsearch() announce (and fs_family_report() record) that m1.threshold is not applied under maxeff, or apply the m1 filter on the maxeff branch if that is the intent.

summary: violated: the selection is plan-independent on the default path (consistency_method = "resample" with an estimable closed form, where no RNG is drawn), but whenever the consistency rate is computed by literal splitting - consistency_method = "split", effect_measure = "IRD", or the per-candidate fallback when the closed form is NA - plan = "sequential" draws every candidate's splits from one stream seeded once while plan = "multisession" gives each candidate its own L'Ecuyer-CMRG stream, so Pcons, admission and the selected subgroup can differ for the same seed. Also at: subgroup_consistency_main.R:498, :793, :970, :994; subgroup_consistency_helpers.R:272, :343, :1492, :1520, :1529, :1733, :1890; consistency_resample.R:76; forestsearch_main.R:3568; subgroup_consistency_main.R:717; subgroup_consistency_main.R:793; subgroup_consistency_main.R:970
fix_summary: Drive the plain sequential loop from the same per-candidate streams the batched path uses (or the reverse) so both plans draw identical splits, or else state the plan dependence of every literal-splitting path in forestsearch()'s own documentation and correct the 'identical on every path' wording for the IRD and NA-fallback cases.

summary: violated: on the default forestsearch() path subgroup.search() replaces the caller's future plan (multisession, then sequential; no capture, no on.exit) and subgroup.consistency() calls set.seed(8316951) with no restore of .Random.seed; further unrestored plan / RNG sites exist in the bootstrap, MR inference and Tier-2 simulation code. Also at: betaHhat_truth.R:849; bootstrap_analysis_dofuture.R:334; bootstrap_dofuture_main.R:352; forestsearch_cross_validation.R:369; fpr_calibration.R:272; frontier_cis.R:164; fs_fdr_report.R:398; fs_mr_inference.R:615; fs_oc_predict.R:233; generate_aft_dgm_main.R:248; grf_subg_harm_glm.R:460; guohe_algorithm3.R:395; mrct_inject_dgm.R:97; mrct_simulation.R:358; plot_km_band_forestsearch.R:349; run_simulation_analysis.R:509; subgroup_consistency_main.R:498; subgroup_search.R:174; truefind_asymptotic_glm.R:338; sim_aft_gbsg.R:478
fix_summary: Capture the previous plan / .Random.seed (and kind) at entry of each listed function and restore them with on.exit, as subgroup.consistency()'s plan handling and .make_candidate_rng_seeds() already do.

summary: With one candidate column the Z matrix collapses to a vector (no drop = FALSE) so the column count is NULL, and with fewer candidate columns than maxk combn() is called unguarded; both stop with the bare error "n < m" instead of evaluating the available candidates or giving an informative error. Also at: subgroup_search.R:132; subgroup_search.R:389; subgroup_search.R:439
fix_summary: Keep Z two-dimensional when subsetting and either cap the enumerated combination size at the number of candidate columns or stop with an explicit message.

summary: When subgroup.search() is given estimator_fn (or adjust_covariates) without a row-aligned df_analysis, it silently scores candidates with the unadjusted treatment-only Cox fit on (Y, Event) and returns those numbers in the usual columns instead of stopping. Also at: subgroup_search.R:138-147; subgroup_search.R:991-999
fix_summary: Stop with an error when estimator_fn or adjust_covariates is supplied without a row-aligned df_analysis rather than falling through to the treatment-only Cox path.

summary: subgroup.search() documents Z as 'Matrix or data frame' and its own example passes a data frame, but Z is never coerced, so a data-frame Z reaches `t(x) %*% x` and a direct call stops with a base matrix-product error on the first combination; only a numeric matrix works. Also at: subgroup_search.R:15 (roxygen '@param Z Matrix or data frame of candidate subgroup factors (binary indicators).'; same text in man/subgroup.search.Rd:41); subgroup_search.R:89-94 (\dontrun example passes a data frame of raw covariates); subgroup_search.R:363-370 (prepare_search_data keeps the data-frame class)
fix_summary: Coerce Z to a numeric matrix on entry to subgroup.search() (or state matrix-only in the roxygen) and replace the example with one that passes 0/1 indicator columns.

summary: format_results() builds a table row with c() and includes the optional fields by per-row is.na() tests, so the exported SG_tab_estimates() fails with its own default NULL subgroup names, and rows of different widths arise when only one adjusted HR or one potential-outcome HR is NA. Also at: summary_utility_functions.R:128-141 (all four c() rows), :606 (NULL name defaults), :617-626 (rbind + column names keyed on hr_1a and potentialOutcome.name only), :518-522 (empty-arm early return always passes hr_po = NA), :265-288 and :391-399 (GLM analogue keyed on effect_a_1 only)
fix_summary: Return fixed-width rows (name coerced to a string, explicit NA placeholders) and decide the column set from the arguments rather than from per-row NA tests.

summary: For GLM outcomes est.scale = "1/hr" reverses only the descriptive arm columns (n1, Rate/Mean(C), Rate/Mean(T), Diff) while the effect estimate still comes from the estimator closure bound to the original treatment column, so a row shows reversed arms beside an un-reversed effect. Also at: summary_utility_functions.R:52-55 (prepare_subgroup_data adds treat2), :195-204 (arm counts and rates from the reversed column), :219-233 (effect from the closure on the original column); callers bootstrap_dofuture_main.R:707-720, mr_estimates_table.R:209-214, summary_utility_functions.R:1007-1018, forestsearch_cross_validation.R:1461-1465
fix_summary: Apply one coding consistently in the GLM table: either invert the effect estimate along with the arm columns or leave the arm columns un-reversed.

summary: A subgroup that contains patients from one treatment arm only is not guarded: cox_summary() returns an NA string for it, but the following km_summary() and rmst_calculation() calls are unguarded two-arm computations, so the whole table is expected to abort instead of giving an NA row. Also at: summary_utility_functions.R:73-76 (km_summary), :540 and :430-431 (rmst_calculation), :518-522 (the guard that covers only the empty case)
fix_summary: Extend the degenerate-subgroup guard to the single-arm case and return an NA row of the normal width.

summary: Supplying the documented optional hr_1a/hr_0a arguments to sg_tables() (or calling SG_tab_estimates() with SG_flag = "ITT" and a non-NA hr_1a) always stops with a base-R error, because the ITT row is built without an adjusted-estimate field while its names, and the later rbind, are sized as if it had one. Also at: summary_utility_functions.R:630-636 (ITT names sized by hr_1a; error at 634, or 635 with a potential-outcome column); 1024-1037 (sg_tables survival path forwards hr_1a/hr_0a to the ITT call); 348-362 vs 393-398 with 1014-1015 and 1043 (GLM path: 7-column ITT frame rbind-ed to an 8-column subgroup frame); 842-869 (GRF-GLM path, same)
fix_summary: Give the ITT row the same width as the subgroup rows when adjusted estimates are supplied (an empty adjusted cell), in both the survival and the GLM table builders.

summary: With est.scale = "1/hr" the ITT branch of SG_tab_estimates() never reads est.scale while the subgroup branch reverses the treatment arms, so the sg_tables() estimates table shows HR and original-arm n1/m1/m0 in the ITT row and 1/HR and swapped-arm n1/m1/m0 in the subgroup rows under the same column headers. Also at: summary_utility_functions.R:609-616 with 52-55 (subgroup branch reverses the arms); 1036-1043 (sg_tables stacks ITT and subgroup rows under one header); 348-363 vs 366-389 (SG_tab_estimates_glm: ITT branch returns before the reversal, subgroup rows swap arm columns only); 1157-1159 vs 1279-1284, 1303 (Table 2 column inverted, source note prints the untransformed maximum HR); forestsearch_cross_validation.R:1656-1699 (est.scale passed to the ITT call, where it has no effect, and not to the subgroup calls)
fix_summary: Apply the est.scale arm reversal to the ITT row as well, so every row of the estimates table is on one coding (and make the Table 2 source note follow its column).

summary: A df.analysis that is not a data frame is routed into the zero-row early exit, so it is reported as 'df.analysis has zero rows' and returned as a no-subgroup result, and with quiet = TRUE nothing is signalled at all. Also at: forestsearch_main.R:1921-1924; get_fsdata.R:99-106
fix_summary: Split the two conditions: stop with a type error for a non-data.frame input and keep the quiet early exit for a zero-row data frame only.

summary: On a slice with an empty treatment arm the risk-difference estimator returns estimate = 0 with se = NA and converged = TRUE instead of a non-estimable result, unlike MD (NA) and OR/RR (NA with a reason). Also at: glm_effect_estimators.R:399; glm_effect_estimators.R:533
fix_summary: Return the non-estimable result for RD when either arm of the slice is empty.

summary: In a direct subgroup.consistency() call with a non-NULL stop_threshold and a Pcons-keyed focus ("hr", "maxSG", "minSG", "hrMaxSG", "hrMinSG"), the sequential loop stops at the first candidate reaching stop_threshold while a parallel plan evaluates and keeps the whole batch containing it, so the selected subgroup can differ between plans and between worker counts with no randomness involved (also under the default "resample" method). Also at: subgroup_consistency_main.R:853, :913, :1005, :1014; roxygen subgroup_consistency_main.R:156-161, :276-279
fix_summary: Make subgroup.consistency() itself ignore (or reject with a warning) a stop_threshold for every focus whose key contains Pcons, as forestsearch() already does, and correct the roxygen that calls early stopping valid for those foci.

summary: subgroup.consistency() neither documents nor checks that df must contain an id column; without one it returns a selected subgroup together with an all-zero sg.harm.id and a df_flag that has no id column and recommends treatment for every subject, with no error or warning. Also at: subgroup_consistency_main.R:75-76 (roxygen lists only Y, Event, Treat); subgroup_consistency_helpers.R:934-937; subgroup_consistency_helpers.R:939-942
fix_summary: Require and document the id column in subgroup.consistency(), or derive membership from row position instead of id matching.

summary: A standard set name that has no patient in the population (for example "Hstar" on a DGM built without an x3 subgroup) is not rejected, and ahr_limit() with b and h given returns a finite hr (the uniroot bracket end, exp(-10)) with NaN ahr/cde and no error, while the same empty set passed as a logical vector stops with "The set is empty.". Also at: ahr_analytic.R:420 (.ahr_fast adds no part when n == 0); ahr_analytic.R:328 (.ahr_core: uniroot on an identically zero score); ahr_analytic.R:621-622 (ahr_design computes requested standard sets the same way); ahr_tables.R:78-81 (ahr_truths_table writes the row)
fix_summary: Apply the existing empty-set stop to named sets as well, before either route is entered.

summary: ahr_design() does not validate b and h: with b = NULL (alone or with h = NULL) every set is computed on its own direct-route grid from the DGM's stored effects, a supplied h is ignored yet echoed in the result, and the nested-set correlations and trigger probabilities are formed from node arrays that do not share a grid. Also at: ahr_analytic.R:612-618 (validation block covers pop, n, sets only); ahr_analytic.R:456-458 (.ahr_exact: `fast <- two && ...`, so force_fast is ignored when b or h is NULL); ahr_analytic.R:289 (.ahr_psi returns pop$psi when either b or h is NULL); ahr_analytic.R:623 and :557-562 (one weight vector applied to node arrays of every set)
fix_summary: Reject NULL or non-scalar b and h at the top of ahr_design(), as ahr_design_table() already does.

summary: For a fit with est.scale = "1/hr" the 'observed' and 'bias-corrected' reference lines of the bootstrap diagnostic histograms are drawn at the negative of their log-scale positions, because log() is applied to estimates already inverted to 1/HR while the histogram is of uninverted log estimates. Also at: bootstrap_summaries_helpers.R:752-753 (Hc plot); summarize_bootstrap_results.R:304-310 (call site that has est.scale but does not pass it)
fix_summary: Pass the object's est.scale to the plot helper and place the reference lines on the same uninverted log scale as the histogram (or invert the histogram consistently).

summary: The helper re-filters its input to rows with non-missing Pcons, so for DINA-selection bootstraps (Pcons always NA although any_found = 1) factor_presence and factor_presence_specific come back empty even though subgroups were identified. Also at: summarize_bootstrap_subgroups.R:107-108 (caller selects found rows by any_found), 469-474 (call), 628-637 (returned as factor_presence / factor_presence_specific)
fix_summary: Do not re-filter on Pcons inside the helper (the caller already passes the found rows), or apply the same any_found-first rule there.

summary: Every forestsearch() error inside the calibration loop is discarded and counted as 'no subgroup found', so a fs_args list that makes every call fail returns a fitted leff_calibration built only from the clamp value, with no warning or failure count. Also at: calibrate_null_correction.R:362-365 (NULL scored as not found); calibrate_null_correction.R:392-393 (zero FPR clamped to 0.5/n_sims)
fix_summary: Count errored replicates separately from non-detections and stop or warn (with the first condition message) when replicates fail.

summary: A GRF result in which no subgroup was found is rejected with an input-type error, although the roxygen says non-detection is handled automatically by classifying all subjects to the complement. Also at: compare_fs_subgroups.R:133-137 (the stop reached); grf_helpers.R:540-543 (null GRF result returns the input data without treat.recommend); roxygen compare_fs_subgroups.R:17-19, 58-61
fix_summary: Treat a GRF result list whose data lacks treat.recommend (sg.harm.id NULL) as non-detection in the same way as a forestsearch object with no df.est, or correct the documentation.

summary: Result slots are filled with `list[[k]] <- value` where value can be NULL, which deletes element k rather than storing NULL, so the returned $fs, $errors, $ci_tab and $plots lists come back shorter than n_combos with names shifted onto the wrong combinations. Also at: compare_selection_rules.R:585 (error_list[[k]] <- err_k, NULL on every successful fit); :603 (ci_list[[k]] <- ci_k, NULL when compute_frontier_cis errors); :625 (plot_list[[k]] <- plot_k, NULL when the plot fails or plot_pareto_frontier returns invisible(NULL), plot_pareto_frontier.R:88-92); :610 (ci_list[[k]] read after a deletion)
fix_summary: Store NULL results without deleting the slot (assign only when non-NULL, or assign through single-bracket with list(NULL)) for all four lists.

summary: With plot_style = "grid", a threshold and CDE columns, the function stops in density() after all computation whenever one of the two subgroups has fewer than two subjects, which includes its own 'no subgroup found' fallback, so no result is returned. Also at: cox_ahr_cde_wrapper.R:693; cox_ahr_cde_wrapper.R:224-225 and :270-275 (NaN AHR/CDE for an empty subgroup, no message)
fix_summary: Skip or guard the subgroup density overlays when a subgroup has fewer than two subjects, and flag the empty-subgroup NaN summaries.

summary: summary.cox_ahr_cde() applies `$knots` to the splines::ns() basis (an atomic matrix whose knots are an attribute), so the exported summary method stops with a `$`-on-atomic error for every object returned by cox_ahr_cde_analysis().
fix_summary: Take the knot count from the basis attribute (or report the number of basis columns) instead of using `$knots` on the ns matrix.

summary: Records with a missing treatment value are not excluded before the arm split, so each one becomes an all-NA row in BOTH arm data frames, inflating the header n of both columns and producing spurious 'Missing' rows for every variable. Also at: create_summary_table.R:117 (second arm); consequences at 148/153, 211/214, 325-326, 333/336, 438-439, 446/449, 548-549, 556/559, 601-602, 874-881
fix_summary: Drop (or stop on / report) records with missing treatment before splitting the data by arm.

summary: The first sorted level of treat_var is always labelled "Control" and the second "Treatment", with the level values never shown, so a two-level coding whose control level does not sort first (e.g. character "active"/"placebo") is displayed with the arms swapped. Also at: create_summary_table.R:107 (sort order decides the arm), 117, 123-124, 601-602, 873-881 (hard-coded 'Control'/'Treatment' labels); roxygen :15
fix_summary: Either label the two columns with the actual level values or validate and document that treat_var must be coded 0 = control, 1 = treatment.

summary: With the default use_alternating_rows = TRUE the even-row index is built as seq(2, nrow, by = 2), which errors ('wrong sign in by argument') when the table has one row (or none), so a summary of a single continuous or binary variable with no missing values cannot be produced.
fix_summary: Build the even-row index with a construction that is empty when the table has fewer than two rows, before styling.

summary: With include_raw = TRUE and table_style = "combined" the is.list(result) test is TRUE for a data.frame and for a gt table, so the raw matrices are assigned into the table object instead of being wrapped in a list: with use_gt = FALSE this errors for a forestsearch_tenfold result and returns a data.frame with a junk list column for a forestsearch_Kfold result. Also at: cv_summary_tables.R:602-608 (assignments into the table object); 609-620 (list-wrapping branch unreachable for 'combined'); roxygen 311-312
fix_summary: Choose between appending and wrapping by table_style (or by whether the result is a bare table object) rather than by is.list(result).

summary: dina_fit_bagged(seed = ) seeds only the bootstrap indices; the per-bag cross-fitting folds (on by default) are drawn unseeded from the caller's RNG stream, so the same seed does not reproduce the fit and the documented 'global RNG state is restored on exit' does not hold. Also at: dina_bagged.R:357 (per-bag dina_fit(seed = NULL)); dina_bagged.R:204-207 (parallel branch: seed = TRUE streams from the ambient RNG state); dina_bagged.R:43 with dina.R:109-110 (inherited @param seed text; man/dina_fit_bagged.Rd:115-116); dina_bagged.R:357
fix_summary: Derive the per-bag fold seeds from `seed` in both the sequential and the parallel branch, and give dina_fit_bagged its own @param seed text that states what the seed controls.

summary: dina_fit_bagged() with family = "cox" and Y supplied as a two-column matrix (a form its inherited @param Y documents and dina_fit() accepts) subsets Y by linear indexing, so every bag fails and the call stops. Also at: dina_bagged.R:385 (call site in .dina_safe_one_bag); dina_bagged.R:149-158 (dina_fit_bagged validates/coerces X only, never Y); dina.R:183 (the matrix -> data frame coercion that dina_fit() does and the bagged path lacks)
fix_summary: Coerce a matrix Y to a data frame once at the top of dina_fit_bagged() for the Cox family, as dina_fit() does (or make the subsetting helper row-subset matrices).

summary: A supplied `sg` computed with tau_sign = -1 is accepted, but the bootstrap has no tau_sign: the fixed-subgroup effect CI is computed on the fit's own scale (opposite sign to sg$mean_tau_hat and sg$ci) and every resample applies the m_diff floor to the un-negated tau-hat, i.e. the opposite tail. Also at: dina_subgroup_bootstrap.R:805-809 (per-resample search with tau_sign = 1); dina_subgroup_bootstrap.R:412-459 (no tau_sign check on sg); dina_subgroup_bootstrap.R:940 vs 946-949 (printed side by side); dina_subgroup.R:373, 435 (tau_sign applied and recorded only in sg$call)
fix_summary: Carry the orientation of a supplied sg (or a tau_sign argument) into the effect functional and every per-resample dina_subgroup() call, or reject an sg whose call records tau_sign = -1.

summary: dina_subgroup_bootstrap() has no max_depth, grid_probs or selection_rule argument and does not compare them with a supplied `sg`, so an `sg` found with max_depth = 1 or selection_rule = "pareto"/"both" is accepted while every resample is searched with max_depth = 2 and the neighborhood rule. Also at: dina_subgroup_bootstrap.R:470-475, 483-488 (point-estimate searches, same omission); dina_subgroup_bootstrap.R:273-296 (formals); dina_subgroup_bootstrap.R:412-459 (sg validation block); dina_subgroup.R:323-326 (defaults max_depth = 2L, grid_probs, selection_rule = "neighborhood"); dina_subgroup.R:618, 624 (sg stores selection_rule and max_depth)
fix_summary: Expose max_depth, grid_probs and selection_rule on dina_subgroup_bootstrap(), forward them to all three dina_subgroup() calls, and reject a supplied sg whose stored max_depth / selection_rule differ.

summary: The within-subgroup refit helpers and print.dina_subgroup_bootstrap() still assume a single-cut subgroup (scalar `if (direction == "left")`, `if (covariate %in% ...)`), so for a two-cut subgroup, which dina_subgroup() can return under its default max_depth = 2L, dina_subgroup_refit() stops with 'the condition has length > 1', dina_subgroup_bootstrap() drops its default refit with that message as a warning (or aborts if refit_confounders is a character vector), and print() of the bootstrap result errors; no reported number is wrong. Also at: dina_subgroup_refit.R:274 (.dina_resolve_confounders, only with a character-vector confounders; called outside the tryCatch at dina_subgroup_bootstrap.R:511-515, so there it aborts the bootstrap); dina_subgroup_refit.R:424, :428 (.dina_signature_mask; per-resample use at dina_subgroup_bootstrap.R:824, not reached on R >= 4.2 because do_refit is already FALSE); dina_subgroup_bootstrap.R:931-932 (print.dina_subgroup_bootstrap, reached with refit = TRUE or FALSE)
fix_summary: Restore depth awareness in the three places that lost or never had it: make the bootstrap print method and the signature string/mask and confounder check work over the cut set (or, if conjunction refits stay unsupported, give dina_subgroup_refit() and the bootstrap an explicit depth-2 guard with a clear message, as the bootstrap had before c6be5ca3).

summary: The ratio-scale line of print.dina_subgroup_refit() is hard-coded to read "95% CI" although the limits printed are the exponentiated 1 - alpha limits, so any alpha other than 0.05 is mislabelled.
fix_summary: Use the computed ci_pct in the ratio-scale label instead of the literal 95.

summary: The loser classification and its wording hard-code the hrMaxSG/hrMinSG key order (band, N, Pcons, effect, K), so under sg_focus = "maxeff"/"maxeffCons" a loser is reported as losing on Pcons although the rule ranks on effect only, and under the default "hr" Pcons is described as "the secondary tiebreaker after N" although it is the primary key and N is not in the key. Also at: explain_pareto_selection.R:260 (Pcons step applied for maxeff / maxeffCons); explain_pareto_selection.R:267 (effect step applied for maxSG / minSG); explain_pareto_selection.R:414, 416 (fixed 'secondary after N' / 'tertiary' wording)
fix_summary: Derive the loss-axis order and the tiebreaker wording from the sg_focus-specific sort key, with explicit branches for hr, maxeff and maxeffCons.

summary: When the selected subgroup is not on the (effect, N) frontier, explain_pareto_selection() attributes this to `hrMinSG` whatever the sg_focus, promises frontier rows "below" that are never emitted, and then states that the frontier has a single candidate. Also at: explain_pareto_selection.R:130-137 (winner NULL -> loser list emptied); explain_pareto_selection.R:467-469 (single-candidate sentence keyed on zero losers)
fix_summary: In the off-frontier branch name the actual sg_focus, either list the frontier rows or drop the promise, and reserve the single-candidate sentence for a frontier of one row.

summary: A fold refit that fails inside forestsearch() at a stage forestsearch() itself converts to a warning plus an sg.harm = NULL return (get_FSdata, subgroup.search, subgroup.consistency) is recorded by both CV loops as an ordinary no-subgroup (ITT) fold with the warning suppressed, so the CV's stated fatal-on-refit-error policy covers only errors that escape forestsearch().
