Also at: forestsearch_cross_validation.R:485, 1008, 1025 (only try-error is tested; error_log never read); warning suppression at :464, :479, :950, :1001; sources of the converted failures: forestsearch_main.R:3310-3333 (get_FSdata), :3495-3507 (subgroup.search), :1920-1932 (zero rows), :3654-3683 (subgroup.consistency error -> warning, grp.consistency NULL, no error_log at all)
fix_summary: Have the fold bodies distinguish a returned failure object (error_log present, or a consistency-stage failure flag) from a clean no-subgroup result and re-raise genuine failures with fold context, as is already done for a try-error.

summary: When the full-data analysis has a subgroup but no held-out subject of a CV run is assigned to a CV subgroup, the one-row agreement table is indexed as if its first row were the CV-H row, so sens_H is returned as 1 (the complement of its definition, which gives 0) and ppv_H as the prevalence of the original H (undefined by definition). Also at: forestsearch_cross_validation.R:1419 (ppv_H, same row-1 indexing); :1418 (sens_Hc forced NA in the mirror single-row case); consumers: forestsearch_cross_validation.R:616, 1171, 1201, 1229; cv_summary_tables.R:232, 402, 557, 668, 756; plot_subgroup_results_forestplot.R:612, 1522
fix_summary: Build the agreement table on fixed 0/1 levels for both indicators so that a run with no CV-H subject cannot report sens_H = 1 (the author must choose 0, per the a/c definition, or NA, per the no-original-subgroup guard and the MR recovery's skip rule) and ppv_H is NA, then update the pinned expectation in test-cv-mixed-and-fatal.R:142.

summary: For a survival fit with est.scale = "1/hr", the two subgroup-table calls in forestsearch_KfoldOut(outall = TRUE) omit est.scale, so the CV subgroup rows are hazard ratios on the uninverted scale under labels swapped for the inverted scale, and the treat2 column / local treat.name that forestsearch_Kfold builds for the flip are never used. Also at: forestsearch_cross_validation.R:1688 (second subgroup-table call without est.scale); :574-576 (treat2 column and local treat.name written, never read); :577-578 (labels overwritten); :1159-1160 (tenfold hard-codes unswapped labels)
fix_summary: Pass est.scale to the two survival subgroup-table calls in forestsearch_KfoldOut, and drop or actually use the treat2 / local treat.name assignment in forestsearch_Kfold.

summary: When the original subgroup has one factor, the CV 'Exact' find metric scores a fold as an exact match whenever either fold factor equals that factor, so a fold that selected a two-factor subgroup containing it (a different, smaller subgroup) counts as exact, and the package's other exact-match measure scores the same fold as not exact. Also at: forestsearch_cross_validation.R:1776 (depth-2 branch uses the same containment test); label at cv_summary_tables.R:418; the stricter measure at summarize_cv_results.R:940-943
fix_summary: In the depth-1 branch require the fold's subgroup to consist of the original factor alone for exact_match, keeping the present containment test for one_match and cov1_exact.

summary: The covariate-any match misattributes covariates when one confounder name is a prefix or substring of another: the disambiguating substr() is one character short, and the final test is an unanchored grepl() of the bare name against the fold labels. Also at: forestsearch_cross_validation.R:1889 (negated-label variant of the off-by-one); :1902-1903 (unanchored grepl of the bare name, also treated as a regular expression)
fix_summary: Extract the variable token from the target and from each fold label and compare variable names for equality instead of using prefix charmatch, substr and substring grepl.

summary: The line wrapper inside format_fs_details() never terminates when, after an indent, the next token has no space or comma and is longer than the remaining width: the last-space fallback picks a space inside the indent, emits a blank piece and rebuilds the same remainder, so the loop runs forever while its result vector grows. Also at: format_fs_details.R:129-158 (the while loop), :144-151 (last-space fallback), :154-157 (blank piece appended, continuation prefix re-added)
fix_summary: When choosing the fallback break ignore spaces inside the leading or continuation indent, and hard-break at the width when no later break point exists so every pass consumes characters.

summary: fpr_approx() requires effect_true > 0 and c1 > 0 before it looks at effect_type, so effect_type = "difference" stops on a zero or negative true difference (and on a zero or negative c1), although the difference branch itself would compute with those values. Also at: fpr_approximation.R:115
fix_summary: Apply the positivity checks on effect_true and c1 only when effect_type is "ratio".

summary: With outcome_type_approx left at its NULL default and no outcome_type in fs_params (the documented minimum for a survival analysis), the P1 approximation silently assumes a binary outcome while the simulated forestsearch() runs are survival, so d_eff, P1 and L_eff_implied use n_min*p_event*(1-p_event) instead of n_min*(1-prop_cens) and a supplied prop_cens is ignored. Also at: fpr_calibration.R:245 (default arm of switch(): an unrecognised type string, e.g. a misspelt outcome_type_approx, also falls silently to d_eff_binary; otype is never validated); consumers of the wrong values: fpr_calibration.R:249-254 (P1), :330-332 (L_eff_implied), :369-371 and :387 (returned P1, d_eff, L_eff_implied, call_args$otype), :413-416 (print), :518-519 and :526-534 (fpr_calibration_transfer P1_new, fpr_pred)
fix_summary: Resolve the approximation outcome type as forestsearch() does (survival when fs_params carries none), and stop on a value outside the four supported types instead of falling back to binary.

summary: fpr_calibration() always computes the per-subgroup approximation P1 on the ratio scale and requires c1 > 0 and c2 > 0, so for identity-scale measures (RD, IRD, MD) the reported P1 and L_eff_implied are computed from log(c1), log(c2) and the identity-scale consistency threshold 0 is rejected outright. Also at: fpr_calibration.R:210; fpr_calibration.R:211; fpr_calibration.R:530
fix_summary: Choose the approximation scale (and the null value of theta) from the effect measure and apply the positivity checks only to ratio-scale measures.

summary: fpr_calibration() injects c1/c2 as hr.threshold/hr.consistency without removing effect.threshold, consistency.threshold or seedit from fs_params, so an fs_params list carrying the preferred spellings silently overrides c1/c2 on identity-scale measures or makes every replicate error on ratio measures, and seedit in fs_params makes every replicate error. Also at: fpr_calibration.R:306
fix_summary: Remove or reject the reserved names (both threshold spellings and seedit) from fs_params before building the call and report the first replicate error when all replicates fail.

summary: The validation simulation in fpr_calibration_transfer() (on by default, nsims_check = 200) cannot run with the calibrated configuration: the inner call is built with df.analysis = NULL and fs_params = list(), supplying them through ... duplicates those arguments, and the resulting error is swallowed, so fpr_sim, n_sim and in_ci come back NA / 0 / NA with no message. Also at: fpr_calibration.R:545; fpr_calibration.R:547; fpr_calibration.R:556
fix_summary: Take the data, null_fn and fs_params for the check as explicit arguments (or store them in the calibration object), merge ... without duplicating names, and report a failed validation run instead of swallowing the error.

summary: The replicate harness counts a failure only on a thrown error, a NULL return or a 'subgroup.consistency|subscript' warning, so a forestsearch() call that returns its failure-shaped list (sg.harm = NULL plus error_log, after get_FSdata or subgroup.search fails) is scored as a valid non-declaration, and a run in which every replicate failed reports A = 0 with n_valid = nsims and verdict CLEAN. Also at: fs_fdr_report.R:368-376 (warning handler promotes only messages matching 'subgroup.consistency|subscript', muffles all others); fs_fdr_report.R:224-230 and :345 (GBSG fallback is decided before the per-replicate intersection, so an empty intersection is passed on); fs_fdr_report.R:380-385 (scoring); fpr_calibration.R:307-310 (same failure-shaped return scored as found = 0, n_failed = 0)
fix_summary: Treat a forestsearch() return that carries error_log as a failed replicate (flag -1 with the error_log text) in .fs_fdr_one_rep and as n_failed in fpr_calibration's batch loop, and have fs_fdr_report() stop (or fall back to the GBSG set) once up front when the inherited confounders or conf.cont_jcuts names do not survive the intersection with the DGM columns.

summary: With a non-default `roles`, plot_fs_identification_involvement() pairs the i-th requested covariate with the i-th of the fixed anchor / true partner / proxy labels, so the legend attributes one covariate's involvement curve to another. Also at: fs_identification_summary.R:314-318 (labels and default palette built in fixed anchor/partner/proxy order)
fix_summary: Build each requested covariate's legend label from its own role, looked up by name, instead of by position.

summary: For a non-numeric subgroup variable, any cut specification other than a single value or list(type = "multiple") silently falls back to 'variable == first level', so the DGM's true subgroup is not the one requested. Also at: generate_aft_dgm_helpers.R:705 (any other non-matching spec, e.g. a vector of levels); generate_glm_dgm.R:278-282 with :310 (every factor_vars column is made a factor before define_subgroups, so this path is taken for them); mrct_inject_dgm.R:538 (third caller of define_subgroups)
fix_summary: Replace the two silent first-level fallbacks for unrecognised cut specifications with an error, keeping the first-level default only when cut_spec is NULL.

summary: The exported generate_aft_dgm_flex() has the formal default treatment_var = NULL and its roxygen says NULL means treatment is simulated 50/50, but no code implements that, so a call that omits treatment_var stops with an obscure subscript error instead of building a DGM. Also at: generate_aft_dgm_main.R:19-20 (roxygen sentence); man/generate_aft_dgm_flex.Rd:57-58; generate_aft_dgm_helpers.R:431 (validation lets NULL through); generate_aft_dgm_helpers.R:459 (point of failure)
fix_summary: Either make treatment_var a required argument with a clear validation error and remove the roxygen sentence, or implement the documented random 50/50 assignment when it is NULL.

summary: The label panel decides bold/plain by comparing each row colour with cat_colours["ITT"], so any non-NULL cat_colours without an element named "ITT" gives geom_text an all-NA fontface and the returned plot fails when it is drawn. Also at: plot_subgroup_sims.R:274, plot_subgroup_sims.R:376 (forward x$cat_cols unchecked, do.call at :438); summary_subgroup_sims.R:109 (cat_cols formal, stored unchecked at :301, documented at :80 only as 'Named colour map for categories')
fix_summary: Decide which labels are bold from the category vector (or an explicit argument) instead of colour equality with an "ITT" entry, so that fontface can never be NA.

summary: For effect_measure = "log_RR", overdispersion = "quasi" or "negbin" fits a plain Poisson model and also turns off the sandwich variance, so the profile's SEs and CIs are model-based Poisson while the result reports the requested overdispersion. Also at: glm_effect_profile.R:137 (validation admits log_RR for overdispersion); glm_effect_profile.R:370-379 (log_RR branch has no quasi/negbin arm); glm_effect_profile.R:417, 460, 477 (.gep_fit_model branches the log_RR label never reaches); glm_effect_profile.R:40-45 (roxygen)
fix_summary: In the log_RR branch either honour the overdispersion choice (quasipoisson / glm.nb) or warn and ignore it while keeping the sandwich variance.

summary: With family = "gaussian", glm_cs_fit() compares the raw deviance difference (a residual-sum-of-squares difference in squared outcome units) to a chi-square without dividing by the dispersion, so the returned lrt_pvalue changes with the units of the outcome and is not a valid interaction p-value. Also at: glm_spline_fit.R:322 (pchisq on the unscaled statistic); glm_spline_fit.R:326-327 (printed as 'Chi-sq' when verbose); glm_spline_fit.R:461 (returned as lrt_pvalue); glm_spline_fit.R:489 (print.glm_cs_fit)
fix_summary: For the gaussian family, divide the deviance difference by the dispersion estimate of the larger model (or use the F form of the nested-model test) before computing the p-value, leaving binomial and poisson as they are.

summary: For a fit made with subgroup_method = "grf", extract_grf_args() omits grf_selection, frontier_rule, effect_neighborhood and selection_rule and reports the stored return_selected_cuts_only, so the list it calls exact reproduces a policy-tree run with default band settings, not the frontier run that was made. Also at: grf_args.R:206-223 (GLM branch, same omission); grf_args.R:130-137 (roxygen claim of the exact list)
fix_summary: When the fit used subgroup_method = "grf", have extract_grf_args() rebuild the selection call (resolved grf_selection, frontier_rule mapped from sg_focus, selection_rule, effect_neighborhood, return_selected_cuts_only = TRUE), or document that it reproduces only the use_grf screening call.

summary: For a binary outcome the closed-form scorer treats a candidate with an empty 2x2 cell as non-estimable, but the glm scorer used when fast = FALSE or adjust_covariates is supplied only checks arm sizes and that y takes two values, so it admits the separated fit's finite divergent coefficient and the two paths documented as the same estimator can select different candidates and return different numbers. Also at: guohe_algorithm3.R:84, guohe_algorithm3.R:89 (the two glm calls), guohe_algorithm3.R:61 (suppressWarnings), guohe_algorithm3.R:310-311 (closed-form zero-cell rule the model path lacks), guohe_algorithm3.R:183-187 and :272-276 (text asserting the two paths are the same estimator), guohe_adaptive_r.R:77, :80, :88 (.ar_coef_se, same gap) versus guohe_adaptive_r.R:107-108 (.ar_ref_fast applies the zero-cell rule)
fix_summary: Give the binary model path (and .ar_coef_se) the same empty-cell rule the closed form already applies, so both paths declare the same candidates non-estimable.

summary: The Cox scorers of the Guo-He comparator accept any subgroup with at least min_events total events, so a bootstrap resample in which one arm of a candidate has no events yields a monotone-likelihood fit whose finite divergent coefficient (warning suppressed) wins that resample's supremum and is averaged into the de-biased estimate and the bootstrap SD, although the package's own Cox estimator treats a zero-event arm as non-estimable. Also at: guohe_algorithm3.R:110-111 and :113-122 (.g3_cox_lean guards and suppressed fit), guohe_algorithm3.R:57, :64, :68-69, :75 (.g3_coef survival branch, same rule), guohe_algorithm3.R:399-401 (finite value enters the supremum), guohe_algorithm3.R:424 (not counted in drop_rate), guohe_adaptive_r.R:61-65 and :71-73 (.ar_coef_se), glm_effect_estimators.R:300-308 and subgroup_search.R:710-721 (the package's own HR existence condition that these scorers do not apply)
fix_summary: Apply the package's existing HR existence condition (at least one event in each arm) in .g3_cox_lean, the survival branch of .g3_coef and .ar_coef_se, so a resampled candidate with a zero-event arm is non-estimable and counted in drop_rate.

summary: mrct_case_study() restores the caller's RNG kind before running the identifier while mrct_region_sims() runs the identifier under the workers' L'Ecuyer-CMRG kind, so the identifier's set.seed()-seeded random steps (consistency splits with consistency_method = "split", the lasso folds with use_lasso = TRUE, the split fallback of the resample path) draw different streams and the documented claim that the case study returns the simulation's H-hat "under any generator" does not hold for those configurations. Also at: mrct_case_study.R:149-152 (the documented guarantee); mrct_trial_helpers.R:41 and mrct_simulation.R:534 (both force plan = "sequential", i.e. the plain-loop split path); subgroup_consistency_main.R:497-499 (set.seed on the current kind)
fix_summary: Either keep the workers' generator kind in force for the identifier call too (restoring the caller's kind only on exit), or narrow the roxygen statement to the configurations in which the identifier consumes no random numbers.

summary: In the planted-region mode region$loghr is not validated, so region = list(loghr = NULL) deletes the default 0 and, together with x3 or region_treat_loghr, the interaction log-HR is silently recycled into the region's prognostic coefficient. Also at: mrct_inject_dgm.R:489-490 (set_var keeps z_<region>, beta_var is NULL); mrct_inject_dgm.R:494 and :498 (the interaction value is appended); generate_aft_dgm_helpers_outcome.R:154-155 (silent recycling); mrct_inject_dgm.R:585-586 (reported prognostic_loghr)
fix_summary: Validate region$loghr in the planted mode as one finite number, as is already done for the observed mode.

summary: The region-dependent effect (region_loghr_shift / region_harm_loghr_shift) is added to dgm$df_super only, while dgm$df_source, the frame simulate_from_dgm(baseline = "fixed") draws from, keeps the unshifted potential outcomes, so a fixed-baseline simulation from a shifted DGM silently carries no region effect. Also at: mrct_inject_dgm.R:568 (only df_super is replaced); generate_aft_dgm_main.R:388-402, 424 (df_source built from the unshifted fit); simulate_from_dgm.R:241-245 (baseline = "fixed" reads dgm$df_source)
fix_summary: Apply the same shift to dgm$df_source using its own region and flag_harm columns, or refuse baseline = "fixed" for a DGM carrying $mrct$region_effect.

summary: The pattern that removes the spline helper columns, "_treat$|_k$", is not tied to the spline variable, so any real covariate whose z_ name ends in _treat or _k (e.g. z_prior_treat) is silently dropped from the covariate set handed to forestsearch().
fix_summary: Remove exactly the three helper columns built from dgm$model_params$spline_info$var instead of matching on name endings.

summary: With confounders.name left at its formal default NULL, mrct_region_sims() hands forestsearch() every z_ column of dgm$df_super, which for any spline DGM (always the case for create_dgm_for_mrct()) includes the DGM-internal columns z_bm_treat, z_bm_k and z_bm_k_treat (and the region indicator), so the search evaluates and can declare cuts on columns that are not baseline covariates of the simulated trial. Also at: mrct_case_study.R:288-291 (mrct_case_study() rebuilds the same default set); roxygen examples that rely on the default: mrct_simulation.R:232-239, mrct_case_study.R:65-67
fix_summary: Remove the region variable and the spline helper columns (names built from dgm$model_params$spline_info$var, not from a name-suffix pattern) from the default confounder set in mrct_region_sims() and in mrct_case_study().

summary: A user-supplied sim_args$entry_var is silently removed whenever dgm$df_super has no column named 'entrytime', because the override list carries entry_var = NULL and modifyList() deletes a key whose new value is NULL, so entry times are drawn Uniform(0, max_entry) instead of read from the named column. Also at: mrct_case_study.R:277
fix_summary: Add entry_var = "entrytime" to the override list only when that column exists, so a user-supplied sim_args$entry_var is otherwise left in place (or reject it with an error if it is not meant to be supported).

summary: An error thrown by forestsearch() inside a replicate is caught and turned into NULL, and the replicate is returned as an ordinary 'no subgroup found' row (any_found = 0, sg_found = 'none') with no warning, count or flag, so a call that fails in every replicate (for example a misspelled name in fs_args) yields a clean table with a 0% identification rate. Also at: mrct_simulation.R:508 (forestsearch skipped when the region Cox fit gives hr_test = NA; the replicate is likewise returned with any_found = 0)
fix_summary: Record the identifier's failure per replicate (an error column plus one warning giving the count and the first message, or stop when every replicate fails) instead of coding it as any_found = 0.

summary: mrct_trial_analysis() does not check the declared rule's covariates for missing values, so a region patient with NA in a variable of the declared rule gets in_Hhat = NA, is silently left out of the region(G-hat) fit although not counted in H-hat either, and makes the 2 x 2 counts NA, whereas mrct_four_sets() rejects an in_Hhat containing NA. Also at: mrct_four_sets.R:126 (.mrct_check_trial checks NA only on the outcome, event, treatment, region and truth columns); mrct_trial_helpers.R:91 and :108-109 (set index and 2 x 2 counts built from in_Hhat); mrct_trial_helpers.R:133 (.mrct_set_rows, same index for the plots); mrct_simulation.R:815 (data.table subset drops NA-index rows)
fix_summary: Stop (or state the handling) when the declared rule evaluates to NA on any trial row, mirroring mrct_four_sets()'s in_Hhat check, or check the confounder columns for missing values up front.

summary: compute_frontier_cis() accepts ci_level but returns no record of it, and every consumer labels the intervals '95%', so a table or explanation built from a ci_table computed at another level displays those intervals as 95% intervals. Also at: pareto_frontier_table.R:296; pareto_frontier_table.R:314; pareto_frontier_table.R:510; explain_pareto_selection.R:365; frontier_cis.R:328 (returned table carries no ci_level)
fix_summary: Carry ci_level on the returned table (attribute or column) and build the column, spanner and sentence labels from it.

summary: sg_labels are handed to weightedsurv as row-subsetting expressions while the validated 0/1 indicator columns are never used, so the default bare-column label, an automatic label for a single binary-indicator subgroup such as '{meno}', and a reference subgroup's display label are evaluated as code, giving a numeric 0/1 row index (row 1 repeated) or a parse/eval error instead of the intended subgroup. Also at: plot_km_band_forestsearch.R:292 (default sg_labels <- sg_cols); :459-461 (Mode 1 label from sg.harm_label); :666, :269, :273 (ref_subgroups display label appended to sg_labels); roxygen :31 and :68
fix_summary: Pass expressions built from the indicator columns (the documented "<col> == 1" form) to weightedsurv and keep the readable labels for the legend only.

summary: When a fit has no grp.consistency$out_sg$sg.harm_label (subgroup_method = "dina" or "grf") a multi-factor sg.harm is pasted into one string before generate_complement_expression(), whose single-string branch flips only the first matching operator type, so the label handed to weightedsurv as the 'complement' selects a strict subset of the true complement and the second curve and risk row are drawn for the wrong patients. Also at: plot_km_band_forestsearch.R:522-549 (single-string operator flip), 613-617 (conjunction collapsed to one string)
fix_summary: Negate a compound expression as a whole (wrap it in !(...)) and reserve the operator flip for a single simple comparison, or subset from the Qrecommend/Brecommend indicators already created.

summary: est.scale = "1/hr" only reverses the arm labels and swaps the two subgroup names: the reversed treatment column df$treat_plot is created and never used, so every hazard ratio, KM curve and summary is computed exactly as for "hr" and the figure shows un-inverted HRs beside reversed labels. Also at: plot_sg_results.R:215, 221 (treat_plot assigned, never read), 245-254, 278-296, 598-613, 629-632, 764-765
fix_summary: Either use the reversed treatment column for the Cox fits and curves when est.scale = "1/hr" so labels and estimates agree, or remove the dead treat_plot assignment and document that only labels change.

summary: compute_sg_summary() extracts the event totals with vapply(..., integer(1), "events"), so plot_sg_results() and plot() on a forestsearch fit stop with a vapply type error, for every plot type, whenever the 0/1 event column is stored as double. Also at: plot_sg_results.R:505 (same integer(1) template on "events" inside event_rate); double value produced at plot_sg_results.R:472, 481, 490; entry point forestsearch_methods.R:621
fix_summary: Extract the event counts with a numeric template (or coerce the event sums to integer) so a double-stored 0/1 event column is accepted.

summary: conf.level changes the column header and the unadjusted rows but not the bias-corrected rows, which copy the bootstrap object's fixed 95% limits, so with conf.level != 0.95 the forest plot mixes interval levels under one "HR (xx% CI)" header. Also at: plot_subgroup_results_forestplot.R:598-600; 1346-1349 (create_subgroup_summary_df, no caller); plot_sg_glm_outcomes.R:317-323
fix_summary: Recompute the bias-corrected limits at conf.level from the stored estimate and standard error, or state the bootstrap's own level in the row label or footnote (or reject conf.level != 0.95 when bias-corrected rows are present).

summary: The documented argument cox_formula ('Optional Cox formula for unadjusted ITT') is threaded through four internal functions and never read, so hr.itt is always the fit of Surv(outcome, event) ~ treat whatever formula is supplied; debug is likewise accepted, documented and never read. Also at: run_simulation_analysis.R:263 (roxygen); pass-through only at :594, :619, :644, :681, :775, :847, :923, :1173, :1199, :1264, :1307; debug: :271, :416, :647, :1175, :1202, :1267, :1309; unused dgm formal in the extractors: :922, :1306
fix_summary: Either use cox_formula for the ITT fit when it is supplied, or remove or deprecate it (and debug) with a message.

summary: On the legacy boolean path (methods = NULL, the default) an explicit fs_params = list(n.min = NULL) is deleted by utils::modifyList() before it reaches forestsearch(), so the sample-size-adaptive rule never fires and n.min silently stays at the formal default 60. Also at: run_simulation_analysis.R:612-615 (same merge for the FSlg arm); misleading comment at :811-814
fix_summary: Use the NULL-preserving merge on the legacy boolean path as well.

summary: An error raised by forestsearch() (or the standalone GRF call) inside a simulation replicate is downgraded to a warning and the replicate is returned as an ordinary 'no subgroup found' row (any.H = 0, size.H = 0, sens = 0, ppv = 0, spec/npv filled) with no column that marks it as failed. Also at: run_simulation_analysis.R:1257-1260 (standalone GRF call, same warning-then-NULL pattern); run_simulation_analysis.R:1195-1211 (GRF function not found -> warning + non-detection row)
fix_summary: Record a per-row completion status (and the error message) and leave the detection and classification columns NA for failed replicates so that summaries can count or exclude them.

summary: In GLM simulation mode the closure that fills hr.itt / hr.H.hat / hr.Hc.hat / hr.H.true / hr.Hc.true returns a log odds ratio for effect_measure = "RD", an odds ratio for "RR", a log rate ratio for "IRD", and NA for every estimate when effect_measure is left NULL (with ahr.* then computed by the odds formula even for continuous or count outcomes), instead of the effect on the named or default scale. Also at: run_simulation_analysis.R:961 (log_scale); run_simulation_analysis.R:977-978 (return value); run_simulation_analysis.R:1108 and :1137 (NULL measure falls back to "OR" for compute_aor() whatever the outcome type); run_simulation_analysis.R:1337-1344 and :1359-1360 (identical closure in .extract_grf_estimates_gen)
fix_summary: Resolve a NULL effect_measure once from outcome_type as forestsearch() does, compute each supported measure on its own scale (or delegate to the package's estimator layer) in both extractors, and stop on an unsupported measure instead of returning NA.

summary: validate_subgroups() evaluates each subgroup expression with enclos = parent.frame(), so a free name that exists only in the user's workspace (not in the data or in `cutpoints`) passes validation, while the per-trial evaluation on a multisession worker cannot see it and swallows the error, giving a silent all-NA column that the validation step exists to prevent. Also at: run_subgroup_sims.R:538-541 (per-trial evaluation; tryCatch turns the error into NULL and the subgroup is skipped); run_subgroup_sims.R:799 (call site)
fix_summary: Evaluate the validation expressions with only the visibility the per-trial evaluation has on a worker (data columns, cut-points, benchmark columns, base functions), and surface rather than swallow per-trial expression errors.

summary: setup_gbsg_dgm() does not put a lin_pred_obs column on df_super, so a direct call simulate_from_dgm(<GBSG dgm>) with n left at its default NULL stops with an opaque data-frame error ('replacement has 0 rows, data has <n_super>') instead of returning the super-population simulation the roxygen describes. Also at: simulate_from_dgm.R:229-234 (n = NULL branch sets only follow_up and treat_sim), simulate_from_dgm.R:310 (reads lin_pred_obs), simulate_from_dgm.R:350 (where the error surfaces)
fix_summary: Give the GBSG object the column the n = NULL path reads (lin_pred_obs equal to the stored lin.conf.true), or have the n = NULL branch of simulate_from_dgm() derive it from treat and lin_pred_1 / lin_pred_0 when it is absent.

summary: With cens_type = "uniform", setup_gbsg_dgm() builds model_params$censoring with no min/max, so simulate_from_dgm() calls runif(n, min = NULL, max = NULL) and stops with an uninformative error. Also at: simulate_from_dgm.R:330-333
fix_summary: Either populate censoring$min and censoring$max for the uniform case in setup_gbsg_dgm() or reject cens_type = "uniform" there with an explicit error.

summary: A strata_rand value that is not a column of the sampled data is silently ignored and marginal allocation is used in place of the requested stratified allocation.
fix_summary: Stop (or at least warn) when strata_rand is supplied but is not a column of the sampled frame.

summary: The benefit-notation inversion list omits cde.H.true and cde.Hc.true, so format_oc_results(subgroup_notation = "benefit") shows the true-subgroup CDE means on the switched scale beside identified-subgroup CDE means (and all HR/AHR columns) on the original scale. Also at: oc_analyses.R:658-660 (call), oc_analyses.R:732-737 (only consumer of the un-inverted columns), oc_analyses.R:768-771 (output columns), oc_analyses.R:919-924 and :992-1002 (G / Gc labels and common spanner)
fix_summary: Add the two true-subgroup CDE columns to the inversion list so every effect column is transformed together.

summary: With subgroup_notation = "benefit" and a DGM that has no stored CDE, the CDE truth is recomputed from the raw super-population after the DGM has already been inverted, so the b-ddagger bias column, the CDE rows and the group header compare inverted estimates with an un-inverted CDE truth. Also at: simulation_tables.R:1367 (interpret_estimation_table: same fallback after the inversion at :1104-1105; un-inverted cde_H then used at :1384-1386 and in the bias-corrected CDE sentence)
fix_summary: Compute the fallback CDE before inverting the DGM (or apply the same inversion to the fallback values) in both functions.

summary: The generated narrative contains fixed evaluative sentences (low detection rate confirms type-I error control; bias is upward; bias correction improves accuracy) that are not conditioned on the detection rate or on the sign and size of the biases computed in the same call, so the text can contradict the figures it prints. Also at: simulation_tables.R:1311-1317 ("relative bias above the true value ... This upward bias ... worst-looking patients ... modestly better", printed whatever the sign); :1439-1442 ("the few false detections produce highly biased estimates"); :1447-1449 ("the bias correction meaningfully improves estimation accuracy", printed whenever hr.H.bc exists, although :1341-1346 already computes whether the corrected bias is smaller)
fix_summary: Condition each evaluative sentence on the computed detection rate and on the sign and relative size of the computed biases, or remove the evaluative wording from the template.

summary: For maxk >= 3 the agreement table labels each bootstrap subgroup from M.1 and M.2 only, so three-factor subgroups lose their third factor and distinct subgroups sharing the first two factors are counted as one row. Also at: summarize_bootstrap_subgroups.R:382 (branch maxk >= 2), :394 (group by Subgroup, K_sg); summarize_bootstrap_results.R:387-391 (maxk passed is always 5)
fix_summary: Build the agreement label from all non-empty M.1..M.maxk columns, as the original_agreement section already does.

summary: Both cut() calls use R's default right-closed intervals while the bin labels describe left-closed bins, so a value exactly on a break is counted one row below its label (Pcons 0.95 under "0.85-0.95" instead of ">=0.95"; N_sg 50 under "<50", 100 under "50-99", 300 under "200-299"). Also at: summarize_bootstrap_subgroups.R:444 (N_sg bins, same pattern); correct sibling for contrast: summarize_cv_results.R:764-765 (right = FALSE)
fix_summary: Bin both variables left-closed, as the CV sibling already does, so that each count matches its label.

summary: The ordinal adjacent-value step calls sample(possible_new, 1) on what is a length-1 numeric at either end of the scale, so base sample() draws from 1:possible_new instead of returning the single adjacent value. Also at: synthetic_data_perturbation.R:163-165 (possible_new has one element at either end of the scale)
fix_summary: Select the replacement by index, or guard the length-1 case, so that a single candidate is returned unchanged.

summary: A numeric two-valued categorical variable is flipped with 1 - x, which is only right for 0/1 coding; any other numeric coding (for example 1/2) silently yields values that are not in the data.
fix_summary: Flip a numeric binary to the other observed value, as the factor/character branch already does, instead of computing 1 - x.

summary: With continuous_vars and cat_vars both left NULL (the default), every numeric column is classed continuous and then removed from the auto-detected categorical set, so numeric categorical variables with 10 or fewer values are never perturbed as categorical although the roxygen says they are. Also at: synthetic_data_perturbation.R:514-517; synthetic_data_perturbation.R:522-525
fix_summary: In auto-detection, classify low-cardinality numeric columns as categorical first and exclude them from the auto-detected continuous set.

summary: test_hte_from_forestsearch() uses fit$confounders.evaluated as column names of the user's data, but a default forestsearch() fit stores cut expressions such as "age <= 50" there for every continuous covariate, so those covariates are silently left out of the HTE test (only bare-name categorical covariates are tested) and the function returns NULL with no message when all covariates are continuous. Also at: test_hte_crump.R:410-411 (labels that are not columns of df skipped with no message); test_hte_crump.R:416 (silent NULL when nothing matched, unlike the warning at :406); test_hte_crump.R:400 (source string says 'GRF/LASSO selected' whatever use_grf/use_lasso were); test_hte_crump.R:401-404 (fallback to q1..qJ, which are not columns of the user's data either); forestsearch_main.R:1161-1162 (the @return text 'Candidate confounders considered' / 'Confounders after variable selection' that the helper relies on does not describe what forestsearch_main.R:3945-3946 stores)
fix_summary: Resolve the evaluated cut labels to their underlying data columns (or take the original confounder names from the stored call arguments) and warn or stop when a label cannot be resolved or no covariate remains.

summary: With tol below 1 the bisection loop never terminates, because once the integer bounds are one apart the rounded midpoint equals one of the bounds and neither bound moves.
fix_summary: Validate tol >= 1 on entry, or stop the loop when the midpoint coincides with a bound.

summary: The roxygen for c2 says the default is 1.0 on the ratio scale and 0.0 on the difference scale, but the formal default is a fixed 1.0, so a direct call with effect_scale = "difference" and c2 omitted silently uses a consistency threshold of 1.0 and returns a much smaller probability than the documented default would give. Also at: truefind_asymptotic_glm.R:179-180 (roxygen statement of the default); man/compute_detection_probability_glm.Rd:37-38 (same text; the Usage block at line 11 shows c2 = 1)
fix_summary: Either make the c2 default depend on effect_scale as the documentation says (0.0 on the difference scale) or correct the roxygen to say the default is 1.0 on both scales and that c2 must be supplied for difference measures.

summary: For GLM fits print() and summary() show the selected subgroup's effect under the label 'HR' / 'Hazard ratio', and for OR, RR and IRR the number shown is the un-exponentiated log-scale estimate. Also at: forestsearch_methods.R:499 ('Hazard ratio:'); summarize_bootstrap_subgroups.R:227 ('Hazard Ratio (hr_sg)' heading for every outcome type); bootstrap_summaries_helpers.R:255-259 (GLM source note describes Rate columns even for Mean(C)/Mean(T) tables, :127-130)
fix_summary: Label the line with the object's effect_measure and exponentiate the value for OR/RR/IRR, as the Search Space block of summary() already does.

summary: For an argument list with outcome_type = "binary" and no effect_measure, fs_family_report() resolves the measure to "RD" while forestsearch() resolves it to "OR", so the estimability-boundary row is reported as inert ('no existence condition') although the engine applies the four-cell OR condition, and status_counts and the verdict sentence count one data-dependent stage too few. Also at: same binary = "RD" fallback, not traced here: frontier_cis.R:138; plot_sg_glm_outcomes.R:151; fs_dgm_feasibility.R:153; forestsearch_cross_validation.R:1449, :1498
fix_summary: Resolve a missing effect_measure for binary to "OR", the same default forestsearch() uses.

summary: The harm null's k_inter is calibrated on calibrate_k_inter()'s default 5000-row super-population but the DGM is then built with fs_fdr_report()'s n_super (default 25000), so the DGM labelled 'target HR_H = 1.0' is not the population the root was found on and its realised HR_H is not the calibrated value. Also at: fs_fdr_report.R:261-262 (DGM built at n_super); sim_aft_gbsg.R:1024-1027 (calibration builds at the 5000 default)
fix_summary: Forward n_super (and the seed) to calibrate_k_inter() so that the root is found on the same super-population the null is simulated from.

summary: The exported argument criteria is documented as choosing the comparison criteria but is never read: AIC and BIC are always both computed and the best model is always the AIC winner. Also at: generate_aft_dgm_helpers.R:1346 (roxygen); :1593, :1602, :1609, :1616 (best_model always the AIC winner)
fix_summary: Either honour criteria in the ranking and best-model choice or remove the argument and its roxygen entry.

summary: mr_method_comparison() decides whether the bootstrap point is on the 1/hr scale from the fit's args_call_all$est.scale instead of the scale the bootstrap used, so for a GLM fit on an identity measure made with est.scale = "1/hr" the bootstrap column shows the reciprocal of the difference. Also at: bootstrap_dofuture_main.R:559-568, 784; forestsearch_main.R:382, 1637, 1881
fix_summary: Read the scale from the bootstrap result (boot$est.scale) rather than from the fit's call.

summary: make_region_model() called with its own formal defaults for both term arguments (x_pred = NULL, x1_vars = character(0), each documented as a valid 'none' value) stops with an unrelated base-R error, because the odds-ratio vector becomes NULL. Also at: mrct_inject_dgm.R:228, :250, :256, :270
fix_summary: Build ors as a zero-length numeric vector when there are no terms, so the linear predictor reduces to the intercept plus the optional band term.

summary: With subgroup_notation = "benefit", a dgm supplied and no subtitle, the auto-generated subtitle prints the DGM's subgroup effects on the switched-treatment scale under the G/Gc labels while the table body is inverted to the original scale. Also at: oc_analyses.R:641-655 (auto-subtitle block), :657-660 (only `results` is inverted); siblings that invert the DGM: simulation_tables.R:297-301, :599-602, :1105
fix_summary: Build the subtitle from the DGM after the same benefit inversion the sibling tables apply (via get_dgm_hr()), with a fallback when the subgroup effects are absent.

summary: On difference scales (MD by default, RD/IRD with xlim_method = "data") the axis-limit outlier test is a ratio test that only works for positive values: when the two lowest values are both negative it always fires and sets the lower limit to second/extreme_ci_cap, inside the second-lowest value, and when the second value is 0 it sets the limit to 0, so CI bounds that are not outliers are cut off, printed as "<x"/">x" and overwritten in the returned data. Also at: plot_subgroup_results_forestplot.R:908, 973-986, 1174-1191
fix_summary: Apply the outlier comparison to distances from the reference value on each side separately, so it fires only when the most extreme bound is more than twice as far from zero as the next one.

summary: ordinal_vars is honoured only for variables that are also listed in cat_vars, so in the documented call pattern and in generate_gbsg_bootstrap_general() the ordinal variable is validated but never perturbed. Also at: synthetic_data_perturbation.R:152 (ordinal branch inside the cat_vars loop), :217 (remaining-variables note ignores ordinal_vars), :20-29 and :42-50 (roxygen examples), :368-378 (generate_gbsg_bootstrap_general call)
fix_summary: Run the categorical loop over the union of cat_vars and ordinal_vars and count ordinal_vars as specified in the remaining-variables note.

summary: The censoring linear-predictor coefficients are back-transformed with the event model's scale (sigma) rather than the censoring model's (sigma_cens), so the stored censoring predictors equal z'gamma_cens times sigma/sigma_cens and do not match the fitted censoring AFT coefficients that the same object stores in cens_params$model$gamma. Also at: sim_aft_gbsg.R:646-647 (linC1.conf / linC0.conf built from b_cens); sim_aft_gbsg.R:652-657 (cens_model$gamma stores the unscaled gamma_cens)
fix_summary: Decide which censoring model the GBSG DGM is meant to use and make the stored predictors and the stored censoring coefficients agree with it.

summary: 28 on-path Tier 2 functions (bootstrap, bias correction and MR helpers) are never referenced under tests/testthat/ (static whole-word grep), for example get_Cox_sg(), build_cox_formula(), fit_cox_models(), fit_subgroup_effect(); the full list is in section 8.
fix_summary: Add tests that call these functions directly, starting with the on-path ones that carry selection or estimation logic.

summary: 110 of the 158 internal Tier 1 functions are never referenced under tests/testthat/ (static whole-word grep), for example .fs_adjust_terms(), .consistency_cox_pieces(), .consistency_adj_terms(), .dina_one_pass(); the full list is in section 8.
fix_summary: Add tests that call these functions directly, starting with the on-path ones that carry selection or estimation logic.

summary: The exported format_CI() documents its input as 'Data frame or data.table' but selects columns with the data.table-only '..' prefix, so a plain data frame input errors. Also at: bootstrap_calculations_helpers.R:206
fix_summary: Select the columns in a way that works for both classes, or narrow the documentation to data.table.

summary: The roxygen of forestsearch_bootstrap_dofuture(), bootstrap_results() and get_dfRes() describes arguments, return elements, seeding and warning behaviour that the current code does not have. Also at: bootstrap_dofuture_main.R:180-181, 186; bootstrap_analysis_dofuture.R:87-89, 144-145, 200, 204, 211-212, 230; bootstrap_calculations_helpers.R:233-234, 247-249; bootstrap_dofuture_main.R:30
fix_summary: Bring the roxygen of the three functions (arguments, return list, seeding, warning behaviour, examples) in line with the current code.

summary: The three return paths of forestsearch_bootstrap_dofuture() build fs_bootstrap objects with different element sets. Also at: bootstrap_dofuture_main.R:621-636; bootstrap_dofuture_main.R:722-730; bootstrap_dofuture_main.R:769-789; bootstrap_dofuture_main.R:905-906
fix_summary: Assemble the return list in one place so every exit carries the same elements, with NULL where a value is not available, and word the print fallback to cover the zero-success case.

summary: With the bootstrap's default parallel_args = list() (documented as inheriting the fit's settings), the bootstrap stops with an error when the fit itself was run with parallel_args = list(), which forestsearch() accepts and runs sequentially. Also at: bootstrap_dofuture_main.R:366; subgroup_consistency_helpers.R:41
fix_summary: Fall back to a defined plan (for example sequential, as forestsearch() effectively does for an empty list) when neither the bootstrap call nor the fit supplies one.

summary: With the default method = "both" (or "mc") the multiplier matrix has nrow(df) columns while dfbeta has one entry per row the fit actually used, so any NA-dropped row makes the exported function stop with a non-conformable error, and an NA event value fails the Cox guard. Also at: consistency_resample.R:62 (event guard not NA-safe); consistency_resample.R:90 and 322 (n = nrow(df)); consistency_resample.R:460-465
fix_summary: Size the multiplier draws by length(pieces$dfbeta) (and report that as n) and make the event guard NA-safe.

summary: 25 exported Tier 1 functions are never referenced under tests/testthat/ (static whole-word grep), for example dina_fit(), evaluate_comparison(), get_conf_force(), get_conf_force_jq(); the full list is in section 8.
fix_summary: Add tests that call these functions directly, starting with the on-path ones that carry selection or estimation logic.

summary: The candidates data frame returned by dina_subgroup() (the qualifying family that forestsearch's effect re-ranking and MR consume) is not described in @return, and it is present only in the found = TRUE branch. Also at: dina_subgroup.R:631-635 (candidates built, found = TRUE only); dina_subgroup.R:481-506 (found = FALSE list has no candidates element); dina_subgroup.R:238 (tau_sign text refers to candidates$tau_hat)
fix_summary: Add a candidates item to @return, stating that it is absent (NULL) when found = FALSE.

summary: The roxygen 'Cut form' paragraph of dina_frontier() says cut_expr is always '<covariate> <= <threshold>' with direction kept for reference only, but the code writes '>=' for right-direction rows. Also at: dina_subgroup.R:1286-1291 (code and its comment); dina_subgroup.R:1278-1279 (stale inline comment 'render the canonical "var <= t" cut'); dina_subgroup.R:1156 (@return 'the canonical forestsearch cut expression')
fix_summary: Rewrite the 'Cut form' paragraph (and the stale inline comment at 1278-1279) to describe direction-specific operators.

summary: Several roxygen passages describe superseded behaviour: the Details algorithm overview, the 'default split-consistency search' wording, the unqualified 'both spellings disagreeing is an error' claim, and the d0.min scope. Also at: forestsearch_main.R:1398, 1403-1421, 951-953, 661-662, 668-669, 887
fix_summary: Update the listed roxygen passages to the current defaults and scopes.

summary: randomForest is a hard dependency (DESCRIPTION Imports plus an @importFrom on forestsearch()) that no code in R/ calls. Also at: DESCRIPTION:50; NAMESPACE:489; plot_pareto_frontier.R:59
fix_summary: Remove the unused randomForest import and the Imports entry.

summary: The documented formal flag_harm.name is accepted by forestsearch() but nothing in the function body or in any consumer of args_call_all reads it. Also at: forestsearch_main.R:349 (roxygen)
fix_summary: Document flag_harm.name as a recorded-only label or remove the formal.

summary: For outcome_type = "survival" a supplied effect_measure is documented as ignored but is never reset, so it is returned in the result, can trigger the identity-scale threshold warning, and makes the DINA path stop. Also at: forestsearch_main.R:2186 and 298-310 (stray measure reaches the bounded-identity warning), 3236 and forestsearch_helpers.R:1446-1459, 1524 (DINA refusal), forestsearch_main.R:3969 (returned unreset); readers of the returned field: frontier_cis.R:137-160, forestsearch_methods.R:438-448, explain_pareto_selection.R:99
fix_summary: Reset effect_measure to NULL (with a message) when outcome_type is "survival", as part of the same entry validation.

summary: The sg_focus = "maxeff" override block and its warning fire regardless of subgroup_method, so on the DINA and GRF paths the call warns that the effect floor is disabled and that consistency settings were overridden although those paths keep the effect floor and never read the overridden values. Also at: forestsearch_main.R:2032-2041 (warning text); 2043-2049 (split-cost warning); 2446, 2495 (threshold_config$pconsistency)
fix_summary: Condition the maxeff override block and its warning on the consistency engine, using the same predicate as .fs_admission_applies().

summary: The object forestsearch() returns differs in element set and meaning across the three identifier paths, and three early exits return an unclassed three-element list that the @return section does not describe. Also at: forestsearch_main.R:3002 (subgroup_method element, GRF return); :2821, :3012 (mr_inference element absent unless MR ran); :3368 with :3733 vs forestsearch_helpers.R:1666, 1989-1991 (df.predict); :2792-2793, :2981-2982 vs :3945-3946 (confounders.candidate / .evaluated); :1925-1932, :3329-3332, :3504-3506 (unclassed three-element early exits); roxygen :1144 ('A list of class "forestsearch"'); forestsearch_main.R:1144; forestsearch_main.R:1161; forestsearch_main.R:1925
fix_summary: Build every exit from one constructor with a fixed element set and the forestsearch class, and document the failure shape in @return.

summary: With use_dina = TRUE an invalid dina_args (for example an unrecognised key) gives a warning and a run without DINA cuts when details = FALSE but a hard error when details = TRUE, because the details printout repeats .resolve_dina_args() outside the tryCatch. Also at: forestsearch_main.R:3182-3185 (the same call inside the screening tryCatch), :3263-3268 (its handler); forestsearch_helpers.R:1101-1103
fix_summary: Resolve dina_args once before the screening block and reuse the result for the details printout.

summary: The by.risk fallback computed when plot.sg = TRUE and by.risk = NULL is assigned to a local that nothing reads, so subgroup.consistency() still receives by.risk = NULL from args_call_all. Also at: forestsearch_main.R:3568-3592 (consistency_overrides omit by.risk), :3629-3633; subgroup_consistency_main.R:384, 1149; subgroup_consistency_helpers.R:1065, 974-975
fix_summary: Pass the resolved by.risk in consistency_overrides (or sync it into args_call_all).

summary: An error inside subgroup.consistency() is turned into a warning and a normal classed return with sg.harm = NULL and no error_log, so unlike the get_FSdata and subgroup.search failures it cannot be told apart in the object from a legitimate 'no subgroup found'. Also at: forestsearch_main.R:3678-3683, :3942-3982 (normal return, no error marker); contrast :3327-3333 and :3501-3507 (error_log on the other two stage failures); bootstrap_analysis_dofuture.R:408, :626
fix_summary: Attach the same error_log marker (stage = subgroup.consistency) to the returned object when the consistency stage errors.

summary: id.name is never validated up front: the 'unrelated id column' stop runs only after the full search and only when a subgroup was found, a missing id column fails late with a base-R subsetting error, and the DINA/GRF paths silently substitute other ids for the same input. Also at: forestsearch_main.R:3726-3732 (same guard for df.predict); :3390 (first use of id.name; a missing column fails here with base R's 'undefined columns selected'); forestsearch_helpers.R:1669-1671, 1996-1998 (DINA/GRF fall back silently to an 'id' column or row numbers)
fix_summary: Validate id.name (presence, and the 'id' collision rule) once in the input-validation section, identically for all three identifier paths.

summary: The MR candidate family is enumerated with only a non-strict size floor (size >= n.min), whereas the search rejects size <= n.min and also drops candidates by zero variance, prevalence (minp) and redundancy (rmin), so the family differs from the searched one in more ways than the two gaps the code comment and NEWS acknowledge. Also at: forestsearch_main.R:3802-3807 (comment: 'identical ... with two known gaps'); subgroup_search.R:610-612 (variance), :615-617 (minp), :620-623 (rmin redundancy), :656 and :706 (nx <= n.min rejects size exactly n.min); NEWS.md:1382-1386 (known-limitation entry naming only d0.min/d1.min and max_subgroups_search)
fix_summary: Either use the search's own strict size rule and pre-fit filters when enumerating the MR family, or extend the comment and the NEWS known-limitation entry to list these additional gaps.

summary: The exported fs_mr_inference() has a selection_rule argument with no @param entry. Also at: man/fs_mr_inference.Rd:17
fix_summary: Add a @param selection_rule entry describing the three band rules and that only the effMaxSG / effMinSG re-selection rules consult it.

summary: An admission list with a consistency floor but no effect floor falls into the 'unrestricted' branch, so the supplied consistency floor is not applied as an admission filter and no condition is raised. Also at: fs_mr_inference.R:678; fs_mr_inference.R:681-685
fix_summary: Either apply the consistency floor on its own as a fourth branch or stop with an error for the consistency-only pattern, and state the choice in the @param.

summary: A threshold in (-0.5, 0) rounds to negative zero and is formatted as "-0", so the coarsened cut is labelled 'x <= -0' and is not de-duplicated against 'x <= 0', leaving two candidate cuts with identical membership. Also at: get_FSdata_helpers.R:534; get_FSdata_helpers.R:581
fix_summary: Normalise negative zero to zero in collapse_cuts_round() (or before formatting) so the label is 'x <= 0' and string de-duplication works.

summary: Several roxygen statements for get_FSdata's cut arguments and return value, and the lasso_selection title, disagree with the code. Also at: get_fsdata.R:52; get_fsdata.R:62; get_fsdata.R:13-21; get_FSdata_helpers.R:214-216; forestsearch_main.R:578; forestsearch_main.R:600-608
fix_summary: Bring the roxygen for exclude_cuts, outcome_type, the confs return entry, the collapse and rounding behaviour and the lasso_selection title into line with the code.

summary: The LASSO cross-validation seed is fixed at lasso_selection()'s own default because get_FSdata() has no seed argument, so forestsearch(seedit = ...) does not reach the LASSO folds. Also at: get_FSdata_helpers.R:242
fix_summary: Thread the caller's seed through get_FSdata() to lasso_selection(), or state in the seedit documentation that the LASSO fold seed is fixed.

summary: conf.cont_medians_force is appended to conf.cont_medians twice, so with collapse_cuts = FALSE and no other de-duplicating branch the same median cut is returned as two identical candidate factors. Also at: get_fsdata.R:434-436
fix_summary: Re-introduce the forced names only when they were removed (or de-duplicate confs unconditionally before evaluation).

summary: The make_effect_estimator roxygen says adverse_outcome is ignored for continuous outcomes although the code negates Y there, omits the count measures from effect_measure, and omits the reason field from the return value. Also at: glm_effect_estimators.R:47; glm_effect_estimators.R:79; glm_effect_estimators.R:4; glm_effect_estimators.R:369; glm_effect_estimators.R:413
fix_summary: Bring the @param adverse_outcome, @param effect_measure and @return text into line with the dispatcher.

summary: The log-binomial start vector is hard-coded to length 2, so with adjust_covariates the log-binomial tier always errors and the adjusted RR is always the modified-Poisson fit. Also at: glm_effect_estimators.R:484
fix_summary: Size the start vector from the model matrix so the log-binomial tier is attempted for adjusted fits.

summary: The converged field means different things across the sibling estimator closures, and the consumers disagree on whether to honour it. Also at: glm_effect_estimators.R:333; glm_effect_estimators.R:441; glm_effect_estimators.R:560; glm_effect_estimators.R:791; glm_effect_estimators.R:833; glm_effect_estimators.R:846; glm_effect_estimators.R:897; glm_effect_estimators.R:972; glm_effect_estimators.R:1095; frontier_cis.R:249; frontier_cis.R:279; run_subgroup_sims.R:366
fix_summary: Define one meaning for converged across the estimator factories and make the consumers apply the same rule.

summary: The value returned as IRD is not one quantity: the unadjusted branch returns (rate1 - rate0) multiplied by the slice's geometric-mean follow-up (covariates, if any, set to zero), while the dr_gcomp branch and the package's own DGM truth use the arithmetic mean of expected counts at each subject's own follow-up, and none of them is a rate per unit time as the roxygen says. Also at: glm_effect_estimators.R:889-893 (unadjusted delta chain), :823-824 and :840 (dr_gcomp), :719 (roxygen); generate_glm_dgm.R:475-487, :676 (package truth for IRD); forestsearch_main.R:296 (comment calling IRD a rate difference bounded in [-1, 1])
fix_summary: State the IRD definition in one place and make the unadjusted branch, the dr_gcomp branch and the documentation refer to that same quantity.

summary: The fast unadjusted closures are not equivalent to the slow ones when the outcome or treatment column of the slice has a missing value: the matrix fits error and the closure returns NA with a failure label, where lm()/glm() drop the incomplete rows and return an estimate, contrary to the roxygen statement that failure behaviour is identical. Also at: glm_effect_estimators.R:1149 (glm.fit core), :1061-1068 and :1164-1171 (roxygen claiming identical failure behaviour), :1090-1108, :1203-1213 (error handlers)
fix_summary: Drop incomplete rows in the two-group cores before fitting, or state and check a complete-data precondition and correct the roxygen claim.

summary: With robust_se = TRUE (the default) any failure of the sandwich computation, including the Suggests package not being installed, silently yields the model-based SE with no message and no change to method_used, so the reported SE of the IRR and modified-Poisson RR fits depends on an optional package without trace. Also at: glm_effect_estimators.R:61-62 (roxygen), :688, :787, :875 (the only call sites); run_subgroup_sims.R:207-213 (documents the no-op scope)
fix_summary: Record which SE was used (for example in method_used or a message), restrict the handler to the missing-package case, and state in make_effect_estimator's roxygen which measures the flag applies to.

summary: The roxygen describes trim as quantile bounds, ps_hat as the raw score and trimmed as observations trimmed, but the code clips the scores to the absolute bounds trim[1] and trim[2], stores the clipped vector, removes nothing, and the method = "none" return has no sw element although @return lists one. Also at: glm_effect_estimators.R:1334 (ps_hat called raw), :1357 (trimmed), :1395-1402 ("none" return), :1416-1422 (clipping code), :1450
fix_summary: Reword the trim, ps_hat and trimmed documentation to describe clipping at absolute probability bounds and document, or align, the element set returned for method = "none".

summary: With ps_method = "lasso" the propensity model's cross-validation folds are drawn from the ambient RNG: the seed forestsearch() passes (seedit) reaches only the GRF branch, so the propensity scores are not reproducible from seedit and the caller's RNG stream is advanced. Also at: glm_effect_estimators.R:1408-1412 (seed passed to .ps_grf only), :1345 (roxygen: seed for GRF); forestsearch_main.R:2688-2694 (call site passing seed = seedit)
fix_summary: Derive the cv.glmnet fold assignment deterministically from the supplied seed without leaving the caller's RNG state changed.

summary: The roxygen of grf.subg.harm.survival() misstates the length of sg.harm.id, the tree.cuts behaviour when no subgroup is found, and the fields of the frontier-mode return, and forestsearch() documents dmin.grf as 'Minimum events for GRF'. Also at: grf_main.R:62-64, 81, 99-112; forestsearch_main.R:555
fix_summary: Correct the @return entries, the no-subgroup sentence and the dmin.grf description in forestsearch() to match the code.

summary: maxdepth is checked only for '> 3' on the survival path and not at all on the GLM path, and the survival helpers loop with 1:maxdepth, so 0 or negative values fail with an indexing error (survival) or return 'no subgroup' silently (GLM), and depths above 3 are accepted by the GLM sibling only. Also at: grf_helpers.R:163, 327, 384, 558; grf_subg_harm_glm.R:577-581; grf_helpers.R:36
fix_summary: Validate maxdepth once as an integer in 1..3 in both identifiers and iterate with seq_len().

summary: The roxygen of grf.subg.harm.glm() describes a subgroup-enumeration and GLM effect-estimation stage via create_glm_row() that the function does not perform, documents inert arguments as active, and its @return does not match the returned object. Also at: grf_subg_harm_glm.R:30-32, 84-85, 92-99, 134-160, 170, 204-209, 215-219, 339-344
fix_summary: Rewrite the description, details and @return to describe what the function does (causal forest, policy-tree or frontier selection, returned fields) and drop the estimation claims and the inert-argument descriptions.

summary: Several GRF steps discard errors or warnings without a message, so a failed policy tree, candidate enumeration or cut extraction is indistinguishable from 'no subgroup' or 'no candidates'. Also at: grf_main.R:269-276; grf_subg_harm_glm.R:499-506, 929-939; grf_helpers.R:73, 83; forestsearch_helpers.R:1924
fix_summary: Surface the caught conditions as a warning or a recorded message in the result instead of returning NULL silently.

summary: grf.subg.harm.survival() and grf.subg.harm.glm() return differently shaped objects for the same roles (tree.cuts type and rounding, tree vs trees, selected_depth vs best_depth, null-result contents, class, rows of $data), so callers convert per type and plot.grf = TRUE draws nothing for GLM outcomes without a message. Also at: grf_helpers.R:246, 469, 480, 491, 540-555; grf_subg_harm_glm.R:623-643, 927-939; forestsearch_main.R:3130-3134, 3155; get_fsdata.R:258-261; forestsearch_helpers.R:1954-1957
fix_summary: Give the two identifiers one return contract (same field names and types for cuts, trees, depth and the null result) and convert at the source instead of in each caller.

summary: Three passages of the printed search diagnostic describe behaviour the executing code does not have: 'GRF sees 1-Y' for a continuous adverse outcome, an unconditional 'GRF sees log(Y + 0.5)' for counts, and an RD/RR search direction that ignores the estimator's Y flip. Also at: interpret_search_config.R:226-227; interpret_search_config.R:172-176; interpret_search_config.R:112-115, 119-120; interpret_search_config.R:62-65
fix_summary: Correct the three message texts (passing grf_count_transform through for the count note) and validate outcome_type at entry.

summary: The roxygen for ij_lower / ij_upper calls them the two-term IJ interval and lists only ci_method = "wald" and ij_residual != "two_term" as exceptions, but when the IJ variance is unusable (ij_source = "wald_fallback") the returned limits are robust-SE limits and no returned column identifies that case. Also at: mr_values.R:136-144 (two_term_ci gate and its comment), :163-164; fs_mr_inference.R:220-225, :755, :770, :1070-1071 (H side); :846, :854, :861-862 (Hc side)
fix_summary: Document the wald_fallback case for ij_lower / ij_upper as is done for ij_se, or expose ij_source for H and Hc (or return NA limits in that case).

summary: The exact-matching path walker and the scalar-or-NA coercion for an mr_inference list are implemented three times (.mr_get/.mr_num, and local closures in .mrct_mr_record() and in mr_estimates_table.R) with only incidental differences. Also at: mr_values.R:252 (.mr_num); mrct_simulation.R:773-775 (num), :776-783 (g) in .mrct_mr_record; mr_estimates_table.R:234 (num)
fix_summary: Have .mrct_mr_record() and the mr_estimates_table.R reader call .mr_get() / .mr_num() instead of their local copies.

fix_summary: Have the two-stage evaluator call the package-level helpers and keep a single Wilson / early-stop implementation.

summary: show_candidate_summary is documented as printing two diagnostic tables when TRUE, but every print site also requires details = TRUE, a dependence that is not documented and that the roxygen examples do not satisfy. fix_summary: Document that the tables are printed only when details = TRUE (or remove the details condition).

summary: The arguments checking and Lsg are accepted and documented but are never referenced in the body of subgroup.consistency(). Also at: subgroup_consistency_main.R:387 (Lsg formal); :101 and :205 (roxygen); forestsearch_main.R:3571
fix_summary: Document both arguments as unused and retained for compatibility, or remove them through a deprecation step.

summary: For sg_focus = 'maxeff' the behaviour described in this function's roxygen holds only when forestsearch() has applied its overrides: on a direct call the winner's consistency is reported as NA whenever it falls below pconsistency.threshold, the pool is still truncated by stop_Kgroups, and algorithm reports 'twostage' although the two-stage evaluator is never used. fix_summary: Apply the maxeff overrides (threshold 0 for the winner's evaluation, no truncation, correct algorithm label) inside subgroup.consistency(), or document that they hold only through forestsearch().

summary: The parallel branch wraps the whole per-batch candidate evaluation in suppressWarnings(), so every warning raised while evaluating candidates is discarded there, whereas the sequential branch lets the same warnings through. Also at: subgroup_consistency_main.R:887
fix_summary: Muffle only the intended 'was built under R version' warning by message, as mrct_simulation.R:690-697 already does, instead of all warnings.

summary: Any error in the selection step sg_consistency_out() is turned into a warning and the function returns an object with out_sg, sg.harm, sg.harm.id and df_flag all NULL while n_passed is positive, which downstream code reads as no subgroup identified. Also at: forestsearch_main.R:3654-3676 (same pattern one level up)
fix_summary: Let the error propagate, or return an explicit failure marker distinct from the no-subgroup result.

summary: The ID argument of subgroup.search() is documented as an optional vector of subject IDs but is never used, search_combinations_parallel() still takes max.minutes and t.start formals that its body never reads, and prop_max_count is a hard-coded 1 that forestsearch() still stores as prop_maxk. Also at: subgroup_search.R:14 (roxygen); subgroup_search.R:181; subgroup_search.R:274; subgroup_search.R:1238; subgroup_search.R:1266; forestsearch_main.R:3521
fix_summary: Deprecate or document the unused ID argument and drop the dead internal pass-through parameters and the constant.

summary: The details filtering summary prints the effect threshold from hr.threshold rather than the threshold actually applied and exponentiates it for any ratio measure, so a direct survival call with effect_measure = 'HR' prints exp(1.25) = 3.490, and it prints a per-arm 'subjects' criterion for continuous and count outcomes where that filter is skipped. Also at: subgroup_search.R:211-213; subgroup_search.R:235-236
fix_summary: Print the threshold that was applied (screen_threshold) and back-transform only when it is on the link scale.

summary: get_subgroup_membership() is documented as returning a numeric 1/0 vector but returns a logical vector, except when no factor is selected, where it returns numeric ones, so the return type depends on the input. Also at: subgroup_search.R:454, 458 (roxygen); subgroup_search.R:468 (numeric branch)
fix_summary: Return the same type from both branches and state that type in @return.

summary: The redundancy screen compares each factor only with the running intersection of the factors before it in column order, so a nested pair whose larger set comes first (B inside A, A first) is kept as a two-factor candidate with exactly the membership of B alone, while the same pair in the other order is dropped. Also at: subgroup_search.R:540-554; fs_oc_family.R:505-515 (population mirror of the same ordered walk)
fix_summary: State in the function's roxygen that the screen is an ordered column walk and is therefore not symmetric in the factors; any symmetric variant would change the candidate family and is a method decision.

summary: The size, redundancy and effect screens are strict (n > n.min, reduction > rmin, effect > threshold) while the roxygen and the printed filter summary call them minimums and print '>=', so a subgroup of exactly n.min subjects is rejected although the text says it is admissible. Also at: subgroup_search.R:706 (survival path, same test); labels and roxygen for size: subgroup_search.R:16, 214, 237, 566; forestsearch_main.R:614; redundancy: subgroup_search.R:549 vs :46, :533, :576; effect: subgroup_search.R:680, 734 vs :29-30, :217-222
fix_summary: Reword the roxygen and the printed filter labels to the strict comparisons the code applies.

summary: Every per-candidate fit is wrapped in try() or tryCatch(error = NULL), so an error that is the same for every candidate (for example an adjustment column absent from df_analysis in a direct subgroup.search() call) is counted as 'failed model fit' for all of them and the search returns no candidates with no error or warning. Also at: subgroup_search.R:960-982, 1004-1010 (Cox try()); subgroup_search.R:1132-1135, 1174-1175 (fast GLM paths); subgroup_search.R:992-999 (missing adjustment column dropped from the frame but kept in the formula)
fix_summary: Keep the first fit error message, or warn once when every candidate that reached the fit stage failed, so a systematic failure can be told apart from an empty candidate set.

summary: rmst_calculation() returns its RMST values through signif(x, 2), so the RMST column of every survival estimates table (and m1/m0 when return_medians = FALSE) carries only two significant digits and the precision cannot be recovered by the caller. Also at: summary_utility_functions.R:556-561 (analyze_subgroup places the rounded values in the table row); summary_utility_functions.R:75 (medians rounded to one decimal in the same row)
fix_summary: Return unrounded RMST values from rmst_calculation() and round to a fixed number of decimals where the table row is formatted.

summary: Several roxygen statements for SG_tab_estimates() and sg_tables() disagree with the code: the return class, two arguments described as doing something they do not do, the shape of the sg_tables() return, and the reach of ndecimals. Also at: summary_utility_functions.R:583-584 (draws, details); 726-727 and 736-737 (sg_tables include_search_info and @return); 719-725 (ndecimals)
fix_summary: Correct the @return and @param text to describe the objects and behaviour the code produces.

summary: The sibling table builders SG_tab_estimates() and SG_tab_estimates_glm() differ in return class, in the argument names for the bias-corrected estimates, in the subgroup-label defaults and in whether precision is an argument. Also at: summary_utility_functions.R:328-337 (SG_tab_estimates_glm formals); 349-362, 391-400 (data-frame return); 617-637 (matrix / vector return); 764-765 (sg_tables exposes only hr_1a / hr_0a)
fix_summary: Align the two builders on one return class, one naming scheme for the bias-corrected estimates and the same label defaults.

summary: The forests are trained with num.threads = NULL (grf's default, all hardware threads) outside R CMD check and with 2 threads under it, and no user-facing argument fixes the thread count, so for a fixed seedit the fitted forest and the GRF-derived cuts may differ between machines and between check and interactive runs. Also at: grf_helpers.R:87; grf_subg_harm_glm.R:465, :469; glm_effect_estimators.R:1480; utils_check_threads.R:22-27
fix_summary: Expose and record a thread count for the GRF fits (the helper already accepts a user value) so that a seed identifies one forest regardless of machine or check environment.

summary: An NA from parallel::detectCores() is not guarded where the worker count is capped or defaulted, so on a platform where the core count is unknown the workers value passed to future::plan() becomes NA. Also at: forestsearch_main.R:2063-2076 (same min(), result not used afterwards); forestsearch_cross_validation.R:1928 and :1950-1951 (max(1, NA - 1) is NA; 'if (workers > NA)' errors); mrct_simulation.R:361; fs_fdr_report.R:218-219; bootstrap_dofuture_setup_helpers.R:30 (message only)
fix_summary: Route every detectCores() use through one helper that maps NA to a safe count, as .default_parallel_workers() already does.

summary: On the literal-split path a half-sample with no events in one arm is fitted with warnings suppressed and its divergent exp(beta) is scored as a valid split, whereas the search treats a zero-event arm as a fit failure. Also at: subgroup_consistency_helpers.R:312 (only a total-events check per half); embedded copy :1720-1727, :1763, :1768-1769
fix_summary: Treat a half without events in both arms (or a non-converged fit) as an invalid split rather than a scored one; this changes the split statistic, so it is a method decision.

summary: The plan is saved with future::plan() called without arguments, which is understood to return only the top strategy, so a caller's nested plan stack would be restored as a single-level plan. Also at: forestsearch_cross_validation.R:332-333; forestsearch_cross_validation.R:840-841; run_subgroup_sims.R:817-818; run_subgroup_sims.R:829-830
fix_summary: Restore from the value returned by the plan-setting call (or from plan('list')) so the whole stack is reinstated.

summary: On the survival path the fitted HR is compared with the threshold with no NA guard, so if the adjusted Cox fit returns an NA treatment coefficient for one candidate, `if (NA)` aborts the whole search, whereas the GLM paths turn an NA estimate into status 5. Also at: subgroup_search.R:1004-1031 (adjusted Cox arm returns the row without a finiteness check); contrast subgroup_search.R:1071-1076, 1137, 1181 (GLM paths map an NA estimate to a failed fit)
fix_summary: Treat a non-finite fitted HR as a failed fit (status 5) before the threshold comparison.

summary: The adjusted search-stage frame uses the internal column names Y, E, Treat and id.x, but forestsearch() reserves only Y, Event, Treat and id, so an adjustment covariate named E (or id.x) is bound beside the internal column of the same name and the formula is expected to resolve to the internal one. Also at: forestsearch_main.R:3419 (reserved-name list)
fix_summary: Extend the reserved-name check to the names the search-stage frame actually uses (E, id.x), or build that frame with collision-proof internal names.

summary: The roxygen says an undetected replicate always receives nH_eval = 0, nHc_eval = nrow(frame), betaHhat_H = NA and betaHhat_Hc = the ITT effect, but under focus = "benefit" the code assigns the reverse record. Also at: betaHhat_truth.R:310; betaHhat_truth.R:623
fix_summary: State the benefit-focus no-subgroup record in the roxygen, or build the no-subgroup record without the focus inversion, whichever the author intends.

summary: 117 exported off-path functions are never referenced under tests/testthat/ (static whole-word grep), for example bootstrap_ystar(), count_boot_id(), format_bootstrap_table(), summarize_bootstrap_events(); the full list is in section 8.
fix_summary: Add tests that call these functions directly, starting with the on-path ones that carry selection or estimation logic.

summary: get_bootstrap_exports() is unexported and has no caller anywhere; the bootstrap loop relies on automatic globals detection, yet the roxygen of bootstrap_results() still tells readers the workers need the functions it lists. Also at: bootstrap_analysis_dofuture.R:238; bootstrap_analysis_dofuture.R:439; bootstrap_dofuture_main.R:285; bootstrap_calculations_helpers.R:259
fix_summary: Remove the unused helper, its man page and the roxygen note that refers to it.

summary: The format_bootstrap_table() example passes summaries$table_data, an element summarize_bootstrap_results() never returns, and omits the required nb_boots; four further roxygen statements in the same files disagree with the code. fix_summary: Correct the example (pass fs_bc$FSsg_tab and nb_boots, or show summaries$table) and bring the four roxygen statements in line with the code.

summary: The documented est.scale argument of format_bootstrap_table() is accepted but never read, and summarize_bootstrap_results() only forwards it, so supplying "1/hr" changes nothing in either function. Also at: summarize_bootstrap_results.R:65 (formal), :172 (only use: forwarded); callers passing it: mr_estimates_table.R:156, 306
fix_summary: Either use est.scale to label the effect columns and footnotes, or remove (deprecate) the argument in both functions and their callers.

summary: grid_step is documented as the grid resolution but is never used, and the description and @details still describe a grid search although the code solves by root-finding. Also at: calibrate_glm_interaction.R:12-13; calibrate_glm_interaction.R:61-63; calibrate_glm_interaction.R:104
fix_summary: Rewrite the description and @details for root-finding with the tol_rel stop, and document grid_step as ignored (kept for backward compatibility).

fix_summary: Warn only when base_args carries an explicit NULL seed, and correct the @details sentence.

summary: When id.name is supplied but the column is missing from a result object, the function silently pairs rows by position instead of reporting that the requested ID merge was not done. Also at: compare_fs_subgroups.R:125 (GRF branch); compare_fs_subgroups.R:160 and 172-181 (silent positional alignment)
fix_summary: Warn or stop when id.name is given but is not found in a result object.

fix_summary: Expose the grid arguments in the wrapper (or derive the step from the biomarker range) and forward them to cox_cs_fit().

fix_summary: Build the legend label from alpha, as cox_cs_fit() does.

fix_summary: Replace both examples with a call using the function's real argument names on data that carries the required columns (as the main function's own example at 72-99 does).
