fix_summary: Remove show_target from the Plot Parameters documentation (or restore the line) and complete the two @return lists.

summary: cox_cs_fit() and glm_cs_fit() call par(no.readonly = TRUE) as their first statement, before show_plot is consulted, so a call that draws nothing still opens a graphics device (Rplots.pdf in the working directory in a non-interactive session). Also at: glm_spline_fit.R:154-155; glm_spline_fit.R:154
fix_summary: Capture and restore par only inside the show_plot branch of both functions.

summary: When no subject meets the threshold, plot_subgroup_effects() falls back to the cutpoint min(z) (everyone in the 'optimal' subgroup) while the sibling cox_ahr_cde_analysis() falls back to max(z) (only the top value in 'Recommend'), for the same subgroup definition z >= cutpoint. Also at: cox_ahr_cde_wrapper.R:198
fix_summary: Use one fallback convention in both functions, preferably an explicit 'no subgroup' state.

summary: For a categorical variable with three or more levels and any cell count below 5, the p-value comes from fisher.test(simulate.p.value = TRUE), a Monte Carlo test drawn from the session RNG with no seed handling, so the printed p-value varies between calls, the caller's RNG stream is advanced, and the footnote still calls the test exact. Also at: create_summary_table.R:830-833 (footnote says 'Fisher's exact')
fix_summary: Compute the exact test where feasible, or make the simulated p-value reproducible and say in the footnote that it is simulated.

summary: The roxygen title and opening sentence call the function a 'Selection-adjusted bootstrap CI' that 'performs selection-adjusted inference', while the same roxygen block, the file header and the print method state that neither CI adjusts for selection. Also at: dina_subgroup_bootstrap.R:23; man/dina_subgroup_bootstrap.Rd:5,191
fix_summary: Reword the title and first sentence to describe conditional-on-signature bootstrap CIs plus selection-stability diagnostics.

summary: The roxygen says format = "character" returns elements with no markdown markers and that verbosity = "detailed" adds resolved indicator values and a downstream-tie note, but the character output keeps the ** and '- ' markers and the closing paragraph holds only the lex-key text and candidate count. Also at: explain_pareto_selection.R:20-25; explain_pareto_selection.R:26-28
fix_summary: Correct the @return and Verbosity text to describe what is produced (or strip the markers for format = "character").

summary: @return and @details of find_k_inter_for_target_hr() describe a classed object with a `method` element and boundary diagnostics on failure, none of which the code produces. Also at: find_k_inter_main.R:43; find_k_inter_main.R:50-52; calibrate_k_treat.R:24-27; calibrate_glm_interaction.R:61-63
fix_summary: Align the roxygen with the returned unclassed list and the stop-on-failure behaviour of the shared root-finder.

summary: The four effect calibrators that share .calibrate_by_root() expose different defaults for the search interval, tolerance and verbosity and return three different kinds of object. Also at: sim_aft_gbsg.R:1004-1045; calibrate_k_treat.R:96-153; calibrate_glm_interaction.R:89-218
fix_summary: Agree one convention for the interval, tol and verbose defaults and for the returned object across the calibrator family.

summary: The returned actual_proportion is the requested target_prop, not the proportion achieved at the returned cutpoint.
fix_summary: Return the proportion recomputed at the selected cutpoint, or remove the function.

summary: Progress and diagnostic output in the cross-validation functions is written with cat()/print() rather than message(), and forestsearch_tenfold() emits it on a default call because details defaults to TRUE. Also at: forestsearch_cross_validation.R:586-588, 849-852, 1236-1239, 1386-1393, 1427, 1467, 1537, 1558, 1580, 1638, 1722, 2060-2103 (print_cv_params, called at 451 and 944); bootstrap_dofuture_main.R:391; compare_selection_rules.R:546; cox_ahr_cde_wrapper.R:143; find_k_inter_main.R:124; forestsearch_main.R:1434; forestsearch_main.R:2697; frontier_cis.R:343; fs_fdr_report.R:301; fs_oc_family.R:410; get_fsdata.R:727; grf_helpers.R:587; mrct_simulation.R:542; plot_sg_weighted_km.R:178; subgroup_consistency_helpers.R:370; subgroup_consistency_main.R:578; subgroup_search.R:163; summarize_bootstrap_results.R:321
fix_summary: Route non-print-method progress output through message() so it can be suppressed uniformly.

summary: An error raised by forestsearch_KfoldOut() inside forestsearch_Kfold() is swallowed by tryCatch and replaced by all-NA sens_summary/find_summary, with a warning only when details = TRUE.

fix_summary: Remove the unreachable partial-failure handling and redundant try-error re-tests (or restore a deliberate partial-failure policy), and drop the Imports guards.

summary: Several roxygen statements in the CV files disagree with the code: the digits headroom claim for cv_summary_tables(), elements and defaults documented as required that are optional or computed differently, and error/dropped-simulation outcomes that can no longer occur. Also at: forestsearch_cross_validation.R:188-190, 710-713, 739-741, 754-755, 769-770, 1272-1274; cv_summary_tables.R:33, 311-312, 637
fix_summary: Correct the listed roxygen statements to match the code.

fix_summary: Return NA for 'Cov 1 & 2' whenever the original subgroup has fewer than two factors.

summary: reset_workers() roxygen says a failed strategy leaves the previous plan in place and that workers = NULL keeps the current plan's worker count, but the code tears the plan down to sequential first, leaves it sequential on failure, and starts the new plan with future's own default worker count. Also at: forestsearch_helpers.R:757-760
fix_summary: Correct the two roxygen statements to describe what the code does (or save the previous plan and worker count before teardown and reuse them).

summary: The print.forestsearch roxygen says that with ci_method = "ij" only the two-sided interval is shown, but the code prints no post-selection block at all when the MR result has no field element. Also at: forestsearch_methods.R:85-86 (code), 310-311, 521-522 (callers); man/print.forestsearch.Rd:35
fix_summary: Either print the two-sided IJ interval when the field block is absent or change the roxygen sentence to say nothing is printed.

summary: summary.forestsearch() (and the bootstrap/CV parameter echoes) print the raw call values from args_call_all as 'Analysis Parameters', which differ from the values the fit used after the RD/IRD/MD threshold remap or the sg_focus = 'maxeff' overrides. Also at: forestsearch_methods.R:385-390, 394 (hr.consistency, pconsistency.threshold, use_twostage echoed from args_call_all); bootstrap_dofuture_main.R:415-436; forestsearch_cross_validation.R:2064-2072; source of the values: forestsearch_main.R:2026-2030 (maxeff locals, not synced) and :2281-2337 (identity-scale remap into locals)
fix_summary: Have summary()/the bootstrap and CV echoes print the resolved values (threshold_config, admission, resolved gating settings) or label the args_call_all values as the call as supplied.

summary: Under a default call summary() prints 'Stage 1 screening splits:' and 'Stage 2 batch size:' with no values, because it reads the user-supplied twostage_args (an empty list by default) rather than the resolved two-stage settings. Also at: forestsearch_methods.R:472-475 (two cat() lines); forestsearch_methods.R:431-452 ('Search Space' block prints NA for DINA/GRF fits: prop_maxk / max_sg_est are NA_real_ at forestsearch_main.R:2804-2805, 2993-2994)
fix_summary: Print the resolved two-stage settings (or skip a line whose value is absent) and skip the search-space lines when the values are NA.

summary: plot.forestsearch() defaults the column names to "Y"/"Event"/"Treat" while forestsearch() defaults to "tte"/"event"/"treat" and stores the names it used on the object, so plot(fs) stops with a missing-columns error unless the caller repeats the names. Also at: forestsearch_methods.R:602-603; plot_sg_results.R:134-136, 174-179; forestsearch_main.R:1623-1625

fix_summary: Check at entry that every subgroup_list element has subset_expr, name and a type of "reference" or "posthoc", and stop otherwise.

summary: est.scale is never validated and its two uses test different values, so any string other than "hr" or "1/hr" (e.g. "HR") leaves treatment un-reversed but swaps the benefit/questionable rows, their bias-corrected estimates and the CV agreement order, with no error. Also at: plot_subgroup_results_forestplot.R:204, 611, 713
fix_summary: Validate est.scale against c("hr", "1/hr") at entry.

summary: For ratio-scale GLM measures (OR/RR/IRR) a finite point estimate outside the axis limits is set to NA in the plot and in the returned data and printed as "NE" with the footnote "NE = not estimable", a behaviour the roxygen does not mention. Also at: plot_subgroup_results_forestplot.R:1151-1156, 1197
fix_summary: Document the rule in the roxygen and label such rows as outside the axis range rather than not estimable, keeping the numeric estimate in the returned data.

summary: The print.fs_forest_theme example runs create_forest_theme() outside \dontrun with no requireNamespace guard, and create_forest_theme() stops when the Suggests-only package forestploter is missing although it never calls forestploter. Also at: render_forestplot.R:141
fix_summary: Drop the forestploter requirement from the list constructor, or guard the example with requireNamespace().

summary: save_forestplot() opens a graphics device and closes it only on the success path, so an error while drawing leaves the file device open and current. Also at: render_forestplot.R:358
fix_summary: Register on.exit(grDevices::dev.off()) immediately after the device is opened.

summary: The 'GLM Parameters' roxygen section says outcome_type, effect_measure and offset.name go only to the estimation step and not to forestsearch(), 'which uses Cox PH for subgroup identification in v0.1.x', but the code forwards all three to forestsearch().
fix_summary: Rewrite the section to say these parameters are forwarded to forestsearch() as well as to the estimation step.

summary: Three identically bodied merge closures are defined inside .extract_grf_estimates_gen(), and the non-detection fill block and the GLM effect closure are copied between the FS and GRF extractors. Also at: run_simulation_analysis.R:1491-1498, :1513-1520 (same merge closure body); non-detection fill repeated at :1009-1038, :1056-1073, :1381-1399, :1408-1425; GLM effect closure duplicated at :951-980 (.glm_effect) and :1336-1362 (.glm_effect_grf)

summary: The effect_measure roxygen and an inline comment of subgroup_glm() state that make_effect_estimator()'s own binary default is "RD", but make_effect_estimator() resolves a NULL binary measure to "OR". Also at: run_subgroup_sims.R:293-296 (inline comment repeating the claim and pointing at the Rd)

summary: The @param entries for baseline, dgm and n say the fixed baseline is survival-only, that a glm_dgm always resamples and that n is required for a glm_dgm, whereas the code runs baseline = "fixed" for a glm_dgm and then requires n to be NULL. fix_summary: Update the dgm, baseline and n @param entries (and the 'n is required' clause in the details) to describe the GLM fixed-baseline mode.

summary: For a glm_dgm the returned object stores the literal "glm" in both design and sim_config$baseline, so nothing in the result records whether the run was fixed-baseline or resampled, unlike survival results. Also at: run_subgroup_sims.R:919 (design = "glm"); run_subgroup_sims.R:862-866 (verbose message prints the real baseline); compare_subgroup_sims.R:117-124 (expect_designs guard compares $design)
fix_summary: Record the actual baseline in sim_config$baseline for GLM results, keeping design = "glm" if the documented payload format requires it.

summary: The deprecation message of create_gbsg_dgm() recommends a generate_aft_dgm_flex() call with argument names that function does not have, and then says to 'wrap with setup_gbsg_dgm()', which takes no DGM argument. Also at: sim_aft_gbsg.R:223 ('Then wrap with setup_gbsg_dgm()'); sim_aft_gbsg.R:805-807 (simulate_from_gbsg_dgm message)
fix_summary: Rewrite the deprecation messages to point at setup_gbsg_dgm() with its real arguments, and say that simulate_from_dgm() needs a setup_gbsg_dgm() object.

summary: The roxygen says a positive muC_adj increases censoring although the code lengthens censoring times (less censoring), and it calls min_cens / max_cens required for uniform censoring although the code silently defaults them. Also at: sim_aft_gbsg.R:760-763 (min_cens / max_cens 'Required') vs sim_aft_gbsg.R:919-922 (silent defaults)
fix_summary: Correct the muC_adj description and document the uniform-bound defaults (or make the bounds genuinely required).

summary: The roxygen calls hrz_crit a log-HR threshold and hrz_flag a harm-zone indicator, but the flag is computed, exactly as the same @param states, from lin_pred_1 - lin_pred_0, which is on the AFT log-time scale with the opposite sign to the log hazard ratio (and a factor tau), so with hrz_crit = 0 it marks subjects who benefit. Also at: simulate_from_dgm.R:108 (return item 'Individual harm-zone indicator'); simulate_from_dgm.R:360-362 (the computation)
fix_summary: Make the description and the computation agree: either describe hrz_crit as a threshold on the log-time-ratio difference and drop the 'log-HR'/'harm-zone' wording, or compute the flag from the stored individual log hazard ratio.

summary: cens_adjust is silently ignored when the DGM's censoring type is "uniform", and calibrate_cens_adjust() on such a DGM then fails with a message that blames the target. fix_summary: Reject (or document as ignored) a non-zero cens_adjust for uniform censoring and stop early with a specific message in calibrate_cens_adjust() for uniform DGMs.

fix_summary: Take the reference arm from a column that preserves the observed assignment, or drop the by-arm reference rows when the DGM re-drew treatment.

summary: The AFT and GLM sibling simulators and builders differ in what n = NULL does with draw_treatment, in argument defaults and validation style, and in the fields of the returned DGM object. summary: remove_redundant_subgroups() has no caller and is not exported, and its filter does not do what its documentation says (it effectively de-duplicates on HR alone). Also at: _pkgdown.yml:112 and man/remove_redundant_subgroups.Rd (reference entries only)

summary: The success rate and the 'Failed to find subgroup' count are computed from non-missing H_biasadj_2 and not from any_found, so resamples that identified a subgroup but had a non-finite fit are reported as not finding one, and the figure can disagree with n_found in the same returned object. summary: When GRF was not used at all (use_grf = FALSE, the forestsearch() default), the no-subgroup decomposition assigns every no-subgroup fold to 'GRF returned no cut' and none to 'consistency rejected', and the table footnote then advises relaxing dmin.grf. summary: which_df is not validated, so any value other than "est" or "testing" leaves the local df unassigned and the is.null(df) guard then tests whatever object named df is found outside the function (normally the stats::df function), ending in an unrelated error. summary: MASS::ginv() is called at six sites with no requireNamespace() guard although MASS is listed only under Suggests. Also at: test_hte_crump.R:66, test_hte_crump.R:107, test_hte_crump.R:111, test_hte_crump.R:176, test_hte_crump.R:222
fix_summary: Guard the generalized-inverse fallback with requireNamespace("MASS", quietly = TRUE) and a clear error, or move MASS to Imports.

summary: When a single signature group covers all valid fits but plot_pareto_combined() returns NULL, `plot_combined_subsets[[1L]]` indexes an empty list and aborts the call after all fits are done; no real input reaching that state was found. summary: reset_workers() labels the plan with class(future::plan())[1L], which under the installed future is expected to be the generic "FutureStrategy" rather than the strategy name, so the returned previous/current values and the messages would not identify the plan. Also at: forestsearch_helpers.R:838; mrct_simulation.R:383

summary: The 'max iterations reached' convergence check tests fit$maxiter, a component survreg objects do not appear to carry, so the check can never fire.
fix_summary: Compare fit$iter with the iteration limit actually used for the fit instead of a component the fit does not have.

summary: The replicate loop combines .errorhandling = "pass" with .combine = "rbind" and never separates condition objects from result rows, so an error raised outside the inner tryCatch() (for example an invalid sim_args name) is not reported as itself. Also at: mrct_simulation.R:408, :428, :706-707
fix_summary: Collect the replicates as a list, separate the condition objects, report their count and first message (stop when all fail), and rbind the successful rows.

summary: Replicate data are generated by set.seed(seed_base + sim_id) under whatever RNG kind is active, so the same sim_id is expected to give different data in a top-level call than inside a %dofuture% loop run with seed = TRUE, the idiom the simulation article shows. fix_summary: Fix the RNG kind where the replicate seed is set, or document that the loop must use seed = NULL as run_subgroup_sims() does.

summary: get_dfpred()'s version argument is accepted and never used, and the roxygen does not say it has no effect. Also at: forestsearch_helpers.R:65-66
fix_summary: State in the roxygen that version is ignored (or deprecate the argument).

fix_summary: Update the stale comment and internal roxygen to the structured-definition route and document the disjunction input form in get_dfpred().

summary: The default-worker cap is applied only when _R_CHECK_LIMIT_CORES_ parses as logical TRUE, so values such as "warn" leave the default at 80% of the physical cores, while the sibling helper .fs_grf_num_threads() treats any value other than "", "false", "FALSE" as an active limit.
